News.title: Andy Burnham says opening No10 North is ‘best day of my life’  – after jetting to Manchester on government plane
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has said that opening No10 North is the “best day of my life” – after flying there on the government jet.

The PM worked from his new Manchester outpost yesterday and hailed it as the “nerve centre” for driving devolution.



Gun cops formed a perimeter around the repurposed Heron House in the city centre where the Labour leader was mayor for nine years.

Addressing staff, the married dad-of-three said: “I cannot tell you what a proud moment this is. I think this might be the best day of my life.



“I’m not joking. I know you think I am, but I’m not. Things are just completely coming full circle here, for me to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning at the end of a fairly big week is just everything to me.”

After becoming PM on Monday, Mr Burnham has unveiled a flurry of cost-of-living measures including scrapping VAT from energy bills, capping bus fares at £2 and tax breaks for pubs.



But all three have been engulfed into rows over a lack of cash to fund them leading to muddled messaging from ministers.

Mr Burnham also dismissed criticism that No10 North was a gimmick and insisted this this was the “North Pole” to counterbalance the Downing Street “South Pole”.

He also preempted concerns about the cost to taxpayers of opening the new office and transporting ministers between London and Manchester.

Mr Burnham flew from Glasgow, where he was attending the Commonwealth Games, to Manchester on the government’s charter plane, according to the Guido Fawkes blog.



Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “It’s all very well opening No10 North, but what’s actually changing in people’s lives? Unless Burnham fixes the fundamentals it will become a gimmick the public see straight through.

“So far we’ve had three unfunded announcements in as many days. Burnham’s blagging it without a plan and it’s going to end up with him raising taxes yet again.”

Mr Burnham has vowed to treat Britain’s low-growth economy as an “emergency” on par with the financial crash.

The PM is resurrecting the National Economic Council first launched by Gordon Brown to respond to the 2008 crisis.

News.title: Shocking moment thug swings kids’ rucksack at poor Chase the puppy before kicking him in cruel attack outside home
News.content:
A THUG was caught on CCTV whacking a poor puppy with a rucksack before booting him.

Daniel Monaghan came out of his flat carrying the blue kids’ bag and then clobbered the underfed seven-month-old German Shepherd with it.



The force of the blow forced some of the contents, including a drinks bottle, to fly out.

But the 32-year-old, from Accrington, Lancashire, was more bothered about picking up what fell out the bag than for his dog’s welfare.



The poor pet, named Chase after the Paw Patrol character, just cowered in the corner, before nasty Monaghan kicked him.

A neighbour handed over the security camera footage, filmed on July 24 last year, to the RSPCA.



Monaghan was sentenced on Wednesday (July 22) at Burnley magistrates court where he was banned from keeping animals for 10 years.

He was also ordered to carry out a 12-month community order with 15 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement Days and pay costs of £200 and a £114 victim surcharge.



Monaghan admitted causing unnecessary suffering to Chase on May 20.

Chase has now be rehomed with a new “loving” family in The Wirral and has been renamed Wolfie.

Previously underfed, he has since put on 10kg in weight.



An RSPCA spokesperson said: “The footage showed Monaghan leaving his flat before turning towards Chase and swinging a rucksack which struck the dog on the top of his head, causing some of the contents to fall out.

“The puppy responded by lying down on the ground and avoiding eye contact with his owner.

“Monaghan then stood on the German Shepherd’s lead and hit Chase on the back with his left hand before using his other foot to kick and push the puppy back into a sitting position.

“As Chase moved towards the back gate Monaghan pulled him backwards, causing the dog to fall to the ground on his left side. While the puppy lay there the defendant then kicked him with force on his left hind leg.”

RSPCA Inspector Daniel Tomlinson told the court: “I observed Chase, a young German Shepherd dog, who appeared to me to be in a lean body condition.



“He was calm and friendly. I was present while the police officer explained to Monaghan that he was taking Chase into possession.”

A vet who reviewed the CCTV footage, said: “In my opinion the needs of Chase have not been met to the extent required by good practice due to the person responsible for the welfare of this animal inflicting physical abuse.

“Thereby failing to protect him from injury, pain and suffering.”

In mitigation the court was told the defendant was remorseful about what had happened and said the flat was too small for him and Chase.

The judge told him he should be ashamed of himself and described Monaghan’s behaviour as “cruel”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking after sentencing Inspector Tomlinson said: “The footage of such a young dog being abused by his owner in this way was upsetting to see, and we’re grateful to everyone who assisted us in helping to bring this case to court.

“Wolfie looks the picture of health now and it’s lovely to see images of him in his new home where he’s clearly thriving and living his best life.”

News.title: Heartbroken parents blame newborn baby’s death on doctors having huge feast inside intensive care unit as probe launched
News.content:
BABY TRAGEDY Heartbroken parents blame newborn baby’s death on doctors having huge feast inside intensive care unit as probe launched

HEARTBROKEN parents have blamed the death of their newborn baby on doctors hosting a huge feast in the neonatal intensive care ward.

Their son was born prematurely and rushed for treatment at a hospital in Ang Thong, Thailand, before passing away suddenly.



His devastated mum and dad have now demanded a full investigation into the tragedy and police then launched a probe.

They allege an inappropriate feast was held inside the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) while their tiny son fought for his life.



They have enlisted the help of the Paveena Foundation for Children and Women and requested an independent forensic examination.

Their baby’s body has since been transferred to the Institute of Forensic Medicine at Police General Hospital for an autopsy.

The couple said their son was born prematurely on July 17 after eight months of pregnancy and was immediately placed in an incubator in the NICU for specialist care.

His father said doctors warned shortly after midnight that the newborn was breathing unusually fast and could become exhausted.

He agreed to them inserting a breathing tube after signing a consent form.

The parents said staff later reassured them their son’s condition had stabilised, giving them hope he was recovering.



But when they visited the NICU on July 20, they claimed they were stunned to find five dining tables set up inside the ward with doctors, nurses and other staff eating together.

One of the tables had allegedly been placed only a short distance from their son’s incubator.

The couple also claimed they were then asked to leave because staff were having their meal.

Concerned by what they had seen, they questioned whether eating inside a unit designed to protect vulnerable premature babies was appropriate.

They claimed staff insisted the gathering would not affect the infants receiving treatment.



Catering workers also allegedly entered the NICU to serve food without wearing face masks or other protective equipment.

The next morning, the parents’ worst fears became a reality when the hospital told them their son’s condition had deteriorated overnight.

When they arrived at about 10am, doctors told them the newborn had died.

According to the parents, medics suggested he may have developed a bloodstream infection, while hospital paperwork listed pulmonary hypertension as the cause of death.

The grieving couple also claimed staff released their son’s body for funeral arrangements before later encouraging them to have him cremated.



Although a funeral was held, they decided to delay the cremation so an independent investigation could examine what happened and whether the alleged gathering inside the NICU played any role.

The family claim a fracture to the baby’s right ankle and an injury to the left side of his skull were found, but his cause of death has not yet been established.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Experts collected blood, tissue and liver samples for further testing, with final results expected within around two weeks.

The hospital is yet to publicly respond to the family’s allegations.

News.title: Putin unleashes barrage of missiles on Ukrainian arms chiefs at exhibition in Kyiv as ten people confirmed dead
News.content:
TEN people have been confirmed dead after Russia unleashed a barrage of missiles on Ukrainian arms chiefs at an exhibition in Kyiv.

Around 100 other attendees were wounded in the strike that triggered a frantic rescue operation, the prosecutor’s office reported.



Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said: “Efforts are ongoing to determine the full extent of the damage and the fate of those affected.

“All necessary services are working at the scene.”



Vladimir Putin’s ruthless forces obtained intelligence about the gathering and struck the site twice, according to reports.

Images from the scene show cars burnt down to their shells and buildings destroyed.

Firefighters work amid the destruction, surrounded by debris and plumes of smoke.

The Ukrainian Association of Arms Manufacturers confirmed a missile strike hit a facility where representatives of the defence industry were located.



The strike is believed to have been in the village of Kapitanovka, Bucha district.

Reports say the event was advertised online in what appears a major security breach.

A desperate message was posted from the scene by Yulia Hershun saying: “There are many wounded and there are fatalities.

“A ballistic missile… My head is still ringing. Thank God… I’m alive.



“If your relatives were at the ARMADA unmanned systems exhibition, please call them!

“They need help! There aren’t enough ambulances!”

According to Valeriy Borovik, the founder of the company First Contact, the strike was likely deliberately targeted at the event.

He said: “I don’t think I can reveal everything, but the attack on one of the testing grounds was very serious.

“Our acquaintances were at the weapons exhibition site.



“So, let the official announcements come later. Most likely, it was targeted at a specific event.”

Ukrainian home-manufactured drones and missiles have turned the course of the war in recent months, putting Putin’s forces on the back of foot.

It comes after Ukraine launched a fresh round of drone strikes on “Russian Amazon” warehouses – leaving key logistics hubs in flames.



On the same night, Ukraine used its state-of-the-art Flamingo missiles to strike the key Avitek defence plant in Kirov, deep inside Russia.

The sanctioned company makes aviation equipment, guided anti-aircraft missiles and many types of military equipment used to kill and maim Ukrainians.

At least six people were killed, 26 were wounded – with dozens of ambulances seen racing to the site.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The strike came 12 hours after Putin held an “emergency” security council meeting with top Kremlin cronies.

During the talks, he vowed to boost weapon production at plants – including Avitek – in another push to double down on his brutal invasion.

News.title: Teacher, 73, charged after ‘using AI to create sick child exploitation images of students on his work laptop’
News.content:
SICK IMAGES Teacher, 73, charged after ‘using AI to create sick child exploitation images of students on his work laptop’

A SCHOOL teacher has been charged after he allegedly used AI to make vile child abuse images of students on his work laptop.

Robert John Thomas, 73, had taught at a prestigious college in Australia for years but was sacked after the accusations were taken to police.



The pensioner, 73, is accused of using his laptop and AI software to generate explicit images of current and former students and staff.

He was arrested on Thursday, months after the A.B. Paterson College on the Gold Coast first reported him.



The college has around 1,600 pupils aged between two and 18.

Police launched a probe into the sickening claims in October last year.

Thomas has since been charged with making and possessing child exploitation material, possessing child abuse material and misusing a restricted computer.

School principal Joanne Sheehy said staff acted as soon as suspicions were raised.

“We notified the Queensland Police and terminated this person’s employment and fully cooperated with Police throughout the entire investigation,” she added.

The principal added that she was limited in what she could reveal while the case is before the courts.



Detective Senior Sergeant Greg Aubort, who led the investigation, warned that AI-generated abuse images are just as serious as the real thing.

“Anyone who believes they can use AI or online platforms to create, possess, or distribute child exploitation material should expect to be identified and held accountable,” he said.

He said using AI to manufacture the material causes real harm to victims no matter how the images were produced.

“Technology is constantly evolving, but so are our investigative capabilities,” the detective added.

He vowed Queensland Police would “relentlessly investigate, identify and hold offenders accountable to protect children and our community”.



Thomas is due to appear at Southport Magistrates Court on August 6.

The case is one of a growing number worldwide involving AI tools being used to generate child abuse material, as forces scramble to keep pace with the technology.

It comes after UK teacher Charles Cornelius, 57, who taught children in Thailand, was jailed for using AI to generate “depraved” abuse images last year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An investigation by the National Crime Agency revealed that the man had more than 43,000 images and two “paedophile manuals”.

He was jailed for three-and-a-half years, and was also slapped with a Sexual Harm Prevention Order and made to sign the sex offenders’ register for life.

News.title: Four men in their 20s killed and fifth seriously injured after car ‘leaves road & crashes into lamppost’ in early hours
News.content:
'TRULY DEVASTATING' Four men in their 20s killed and fifth seriously injured after car ‘leaves road & crashes into lamppost’ in early hours

FOUR men have been killed in a horror crash – with a fifth rushed to hospital.

A black Seat Cupra came off the road after colliding with a lamppost in Huyton, Merseyside, in the early hours of this morning.

Emergency crews scrambled to Liverpool Road at around 2am, with two men, aged 23, and two others, aged 24 and 26, pronounced dead at the scene.

Their next of kin have been informed and will be supported by specially trained officers.





A 27-year-old man, who was a passenger inside the car, has been taken to hospital where he remains in a stable condition.

A police scene is in place as part of the initial stages of the investigation.

The car was travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley at the time of the crash.

Road closures are likely to remain in place over the weekend.



Superintendent Paul Holden said: “First and foremost our thoughts are with the family of the four men who sadly lost their lives.

“Their families have been informed and are being supported by our specially trained family liaison officers.

“This is a truly devastating moment for their families and loved ones, and it is now our priority to get answers for them on how the collision occurred.

“We know this happened very early this morning, but if anyone saw what happened or were driving through the area just before the incident occurred then please get in touch.



“Similarly, if you live in the area and have doorbell footage of the black Seat Cupra or the incident itself, please contact us.

“You may have information or footage that would be useful to our investigation.”

News.title: Rain FINALLY on the way this weekend to end 36-day dry spell – but temps hit 30C as heat health alerts kick in
News.content:
SOAK IT UP Rain FINALLY on the way this weekend to end 36-day dry spell – but temps hit 30C as heat health alerts kick in

BRITS will finally see showers after a 36-day dry spell – but other parts of the country will continue to bask in 30C temperatures.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued alerts across Britain, despite many reaching for brollies for the first time in over a month.



While June has been wetter than average for the UK, this weekend’s rainfall is likely to double what we’ve seen so far in certain areas since mid-June.

But yellow heat health alerts for the East and West Midlands, East of England, London, South East and South West will remain in place from 9am on Friday until 9am on Sunday.



Conditions are expected to remain warm and balmy across most parts of the UK on Friday – reaching 30C across southern and southwestern regions.

The Met Office has announced a shift in conditions moving into the weekend however, as a long-standing area of high pressure yields to more unsettled weather.





As the high pressure moves westwards, jet streams will move over the UK, ushering in new weather fronts.

Northern Ireland, northern England and north Wales will see around 5-10mm of showers over Saturday and Sunday.

Western Scotland will be significantly wetter, with 10-20mm of rainfall expected over higher terrains.

In the Midlands, southern and east of England, rain will be lighter and patchier, with just a few millimetres forecast.

It may provide some temporary relief to gardens and parks but it is not expected to significantly alleviate widespread drought.



Met Office chief forecaster, Steve Willington, said: “The high pressure has been a key feature of the UK’s weather forecast over the last few weeks, bringing above-average temperatures and extremely dry conditions for many.

“However, we will begin to see a modest change as a weak weather front pushes south across the UK on Saturday bringing some much-needed rain, albeit it light and mainly concentrated in the north and west.

“Behind the front a showery air mass will bring potentially heavy showers some of which may be thundery.”

The showers will follow months of record-breaking dry conditions, wildfires and scorched riverbeds.

It comes as drought was declared in North Wales and the Upper Severn, which led to a hosepipe ban that impacted over 23 million Brits.

News.title: Nuclear sub commander jailed for sexually assaulting young sailor who woke up on Navy base crying ‘I’ve been raped’
News.content:
SICK ATTACK Nuclear sub commander jailed for sexually assaulting young sailor who woke up on Navy base crying ‘I’ve been raped’

A DISGRACED nuclear submarine commander has been jailed for sexually assaulting a young sailor at a Navy base.

Lieutenant Commander John Cursiter, 46, was convicted of sexual assault, false imprisonment and possession of cocaine at a court martial in Catterick.



He plied his victim with booze and cocaine before luring him back to his bedroom in the officer’s mess at HMNB Devonport.

The terrified victim told the court martial that he woke up in horror in the officer’s bed.



Cursiter then refused to allow the junior submariner to leave.

When the sailor eventually fled he let out a “howling cry” and told telling a member of staff on base: “I think I have been raped”.



A court martial board at Catterick Military Court in North Yorkshire, found Cursiter, of Balloch, Dunbartonshire, guilty of sexual assault, false imprisonment and possession of cocaine, which was found in his coat pocket on his arrest.

He has now been jailed for 33 months for the “planned and predatory assault”.

Cursiter was marched off his permanent base at Faslane on the Clyde – the home of Britain’s nuclear submarine unit – in disgrace by Royal Military Police.

The fiend, a former deputy commander of the nuclear-armed sub HMS Vanguard, quit the navy after his arrest.



When news of the police action was broken by The Sun, a second former Royal Navy rating came forward to say he too had been sexually assaulted by Cursiter after a night of heavy drinking near Faslane in 2013.

Cursiter denied the offences ever happened and was cleared of three counts of sexual assault against the second complainant by the court martial board.

He will be sentenced for the 2022 incidents in July and faces up to six months in prison for his crimes, which were described as a “breach of trust” in his position as a senior officer.

The sexual assaults followed a night out in Plymouth involving officers and submariners



The sailor, who has since left the Navy, told the court: “I am a straight guy, I have been with my partner for many years and I had only ever spoken to John Cursiter on that day.

“To wake up in his bed made me think I did not trust him. I woke up in boxers, socks and a T-shirt, everything just did not line up.”

At first Cursiter prevented him from leaving the room when he tried to leave, holding him by his hand and telling him: “You’re off work today.”

But when he did leave the room, the younger man said his head only cleared as he got out into the parade square and he suspected he had been given drugs, which was later confirmed in toxicology tests.

He told a cleaner at the base: “I think I have been raped.”



The complainant told the court of his fears about being drummed out of the navy if drugs were found in his system.

He said: “I knew if he had given it to me in a drink it would be in my system, but I have no memory of how it would have happened.

“The Navy was my first option, my second and last option, it was all I had thought about since I was a child. I have never taken drugs in my life.”

After the matter was reported to the military police Cursiter was arrested and a packet containing the remnants of cocaine were found in his coat pocket. His DNA was also found in his alleged victim’s underwear.

A cleaner in the junior ratings mess at HMS Drake encountered the young submariner in a kitchen after he’d left Cursiter’s quarters – describing how he let out a “horrific howl” and was contemplating hanging himself.



In a statement, Kerry White said: “He looked really rough, he walked over and slumped in a chair. He was completely zoned out as if he was processing something in his head.

“He was slumped and crying, his eyes were streaming and red raw.

“He said ‘I think I have been raped.’ He kept saying ‘He would not let me go.’

“He told me not to go into his room as he would be hanging. I kept telling him not to say that as it was worrying me.

“He was repeating ‘I don’t know what happened, I don’t know what happened’ and said ‘I’m meant to be a man.’ He was crying about his girlfriend and said several times ‘I am not gay.’



He asked another member of staff: “Have you ever known a man to be violated? I think I was raped.”

Ms White added: “He let out a horrific howling cry as he entered his room.”

The complainant in the alleged attack in 2013 told the court martial: “I felt violated. I was confused, disgusted, embarrassed and ashamed. I was trying to understand what happened and why it happened to me.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I knew he was gay, everyone on board knew he was gay and no one cared. I am not gay and I wanted to know why he would hit on me when he knew I was straight.”

However the Board accepted Cursiter’s case that no sexual assault took place and he was cleared of offences relating to the 2013 incident.

News.title: Playstation down updates: Thousands of gamers frustrated as unable to connect
News.content:
Gamers have been unable to connect to Playstation

More than 5,000 reports of outages have been were logged on Downdetector by people trying to access Playstation with most unable to connect to the server

Playstation down updates: Thousands of gamers frustrated as unable to connect

Thousands of Brits have reported a Playstation outage with most unable to connect to the server.

More than 5,000 reports of issues were logged by users in the UK by lunchtime today on Downdetector which tracks real-time online status.

Some gamers are able to access the Playstation Store but have an error when trying to buy a new game while others claim they cannot access digital games in their libraries.

One UK user wrote on Downdetector: "Can't load any digital games at all bought or free. Can't connect to servers to verify licences, doesn't matter what i try to load i get the same message every time."

News.title: Man killed in crash saves seven lives by donating his organs
News.content:
Man killed in crash saves seven lives by donating his organs

Trainee plumber Edward Pearce, who bravely signed up as a bone marrow donor when he was just four years old, has saved seven lives after being fatally injured during a horror car crash

View 2 Images Edward's organ donation has saved seven lives (Image: Sussex Police )

The tragic death of a 20-year-old trainee plumber has saved seven lives after it emerged that he was a registered organ donor. Edward Pearce, from Heathfield in East Sussex, was travelling to work when he suffered fatal injuries in a car crash.

‌



Edward, known to family and friends as Bunty, was driving in his white Volkswagen Caddy van on the A27 westbound near Pevensey. It was involved in a fatal collision with a white Mercedes Sprinter, just before 6.30am on Monday, July 13.

‌



Edward’s older brother William died from leukaemia in 2012, and after William’s diagnosis Edward – who was only four years old at the time – bravely signed up as a bone-marrow donor.

‌



In the wake of Edward’s death, his family has revealed that he donated his organs, helping seven people in urgent need of transplants.

"Even in passing, Edward's kindness and compassion have given others the precious gift of life, creating a legacy that will endure for generations," they said in a statement.

View 2 Images The A27 was closed for several hours following the incident (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The statement from Edward’s family continued: “Edward was a much-loved son, family member, and friend. He lived life with boundless energy.

“His days were always filled with purpose, laughter, and adventure. He brought warmth, energy, and kindness to everyone around him, and had a remarkable ability to make people feel at ease.

“While this loss is unimaginable for us, we take comfort in the love Edward shared throughout his life and the lasting impact he had on so many people.

‌



“Those who knew Edward were touched by his generous spirit, and it was impossible not to be drawn to his infectious smile and caring nature.”

The family said that Edward was training to be a plumber and had hoped to work in Australia.

They added: “During William’s illness, Edward selflessly became a bone marrow donor at the age of four for his big brother. It was a gift that reflected the depth of his love and compassion.

‌



“In keeping with his generous character, Edward became an organ donor. Through this selfless gift, he was able to donate six organs, helping to save the lives of seven people who were in urgent need of transplants.

“Even in passing, Edward’s kindness and compassion have given others the precious gift of life, creating a legacy that will endure for generations.

“Edward will be deeply missed by all who knew and loved him. His memory will live on in the countless lives he touched, the happiness he brought to others, and the extraordinary gifts he gave to those he never met.”

Article continues below

Sussex Police have said that a 31-year-old has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. He has been bailed, pending further enquiries.

Police are appealing for any motorists who passed the VW Caddy van which had broken down in the westbound carriageway to come forward, as well as anyone with dashcam footage in the area at the time. Anyone who was on or near the A27 who might have information about the incident is asked to report it to Sussex Police, quoting Operation Wickham.

News.title: I tried the 20p kitchen smell hack - and it really worked
News.content:
I tried the 20p kitchen smell hack - and it really worked

If your kitchen seems to smell no matter how much you've cleaned it, try this

View 3 Images My kitchen smells great (Image: Sophie Buchan)

Our homes can quickly start to smell a bit stale, especially in the warm weather we’ve had lately. It’s even worse if dishes are left unwashed or food’s been sitting out.

‌



My kitchen smelled bad, and our fish and chips dinner didn't help. Sadly, opening the windows, using air freshener and wiping the worktops wasn’t enough, so I tried the 20p lemon hack. And it actually did the trick.

‌



In many UK supermarkets, a single lemon can cost as little as 20p. Multi-packs of four or five are often available for under £1. I discovered through multiple sources - TikTok, cleaning groups, Reddit - that taking lemon slices and placing them in a pan on the hob works a treat.

‌



To put an end to my smelly kitchen, I boiled water in my kettle, poured it into a pan and simmered water with lemon slices for 15 minutes.

View 3 Images Lemon slices simmered on the hob for 15 minutes helped tackle lingering cooking smells. (Image: Sophie Buchan)

It's said to freshen the air naturally and work fast. And it really did. After 15 minutes of boiling my lemon water, my kitchen smelled fresh.

‌



People suggest adding herbs or essential oils, creating a home signature scent. But I wanted to keep it simple.

Great options for those wanting to add herbs include rosemary, mint, eucalyptus and thyme. For an extra fresh, clean scent, try adding oils like eucalyptus, tea tree, grapefruit or bergamot.

Clean your hob

View 3 Images A single lemon can cost as little as 20p and it could be the secret to a fresher-smelling kitchen (Image: Sophie Buchan)

‌



That's not all you can use lemons for. Experts at Morphy Richards, urge people to grab a lemon, some hot water, a little bit of soap and some bicarbonate of soda. And before you know it, you'll have a sparking hob.

The experts suggest: "Remove all of your hob rings and place them in a large bowl. Halve a lemon and add it to the bowl, giving them a squeeze so there's some juice in the bowl.

"Add 1/3 - 1/2 a cup of bicarbonate of soda before pouring boiling water over the top - enough to cover the discs. Leave to work it's magic for around 20 minutes."

Article continues below

While they soak, wipe the hob with hot, soapy water to lift any loose dirt. Then pour away the dirty water and wash the rings in warm, soapy water.

News.title: Gianni Infantino accused of contempt as scale of World Cup private jet travel emerges
News.content:
If you took any more than a passing interest in the World Cup this summer you will have seen Gianni Infantino. Really, you couldn't miss him; the FIFA president was almost ubiquitous.

No matter where the 104 matches were being played, the bald head of the head of football's governing body seemed to be there, shining back at you out of the TV.

In fact, Infantino managed to personally attend 44 matches between the World Cup opener on June 11 and the final between Spain and Argentina on July 19. That is more than one per day, despite the World Cup being spread across 16 cities in three countries.

Logistically speaking, it is an impressive achievement, and thanks to an agreement with the Host Broadcast Service (which is 49 per cent owned by FIFA) that meant a "dignitary shot" was mandatory in every half, his efforts were rewarded with regular airtime. The 56-year-old wanted to be front and centre of the biggest World Cup of all time and, in achieving his personal goal, he was successful, visiting every host city.

‌



Infantino wanted to network. He wanted to rub shoulders with US President Donald Trump, with the governor of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund Yasir Al-Rumayyan, with countless world leaders and the heads of FIFA member associations in the posh seats.

FIFA accused of environmental negligence as extent of 2026 World Cup pollution becomes clear READ MORE :

His efforts helped firm up his control of FIFA, with the Guardian reporting that Infantino has the formal endorsement of more than 200 members for re-election as president. Even the scandal of Trump interfering with FIFA protocols to help US striker Folarin Balogun's red card be overturned couldn't diminish Infantino's standing.

Yet the method by which Infantino achieved all of this - plus a reported endorsement from Trump to become the next United Nations secretary general - casts a long shadow over the whole charade: a Qatar Airways-sponsored private jet.

Flight data shows that Infantino covered 106,323 km (66,066 miles) - almost three times the Earth's circumference - during the World Cup in a private Gulfstream G650, burning 1,020.3 tonnes of CO₂e in the process.

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino used the World Cup as a networking event (Image: Eva Marie Uzcategui/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA's decision to expand the tournament to 48 teams and spread it over three countries made it the most polluting World Cup in history right off the bat, with predicted emissions of nine million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e), almost double the historical average from previous tournaments between 2010 and 2022. The vast majority of those emissions come from air travel.

FIFA has pledged to cut green house gas emissions 50 per cent by 2030 and reach net zero by 2040, while Infantino promised to leave a "positive footprint" on North America. Campaigners believe that his actions speak louder than his words.

“As players and supporters struggled through extreme heat, Infantino’s Qatari private jet took him from VIP box to VIP box across his bloated tournament," said Frank Huisingh, founder of Fossil Free Football. "There could be no more perfect illustration for FIFA’s wilful blindness to the climate threats facing football and its fans."

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino, pictured in 2017, has regularly travelled by Qatar executive jet (Image: ISAAC KASAMANI/AFP via Getty Images)

Katie Cross, chief executive of sports sustainability charity Pledgeball, said: “The incredible emissions generated by Infantino’s private jet usage, against a backdrop of heat waves, wild fires and fans priced out of the World Cup, smack of a complete disregard for the longevity of the game, the players and the fans who make it.”

Andrew Simms, director of New Weather Institute, said Infantino's jet left behind " a cloud of contempt", while Freddie Daley, of the Cool Down Sport for Climate Action Network, noted that "it is further evidence that he and FIFA cannot be trusted to protect the game from a worsening climate crisis.”

Jenny Amann, a doctoral researcher at Loughborough University, has been interviewing fans about the relationship between climate change and football and has consistently heard negative reviews of the FIFA president.

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino managed to shake a lot of hands at a huge environmental cost (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"I cannot recall a single interview in which Infantino’s actions and decision-making were not criticised," she said. "Fans consistently describe his approach as absurd and hypocritical, expressing frustration at being asked to adopt more climate-friendly behaviours while international football and its leaders continue to operate in a way that is totally detached from the broader societal crises we face.

"Infantino's travel choices at this tournament will generate emissions hundreds of times greater than the average European football fan produces in an entire year. Actions like these will do nothing to encourage fans towards more sustainable behaviours - and they suggest neither Infantino nor FIFA has any intention of leading by example.”

There is a sense of incredulity behind the scenes at FIFA at the criticism of Infantino, with the common defence being he couldn't have just watched the tournament from an office in Miami. Infantino is keen to present himself as the opposite of UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin, who was criticised last summer for only attending two matches at the Women's Euros.

‌



When asked about Infantinio's private jet usage and the environmental concerns it raised, a FIFA spokesperson said: “As we have consistently stated, FIFA has put in place rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any FIFA official. The FIFA president routinely travels, together with relevant officials, on business and tournament-related matters and strives to visit member associations of FIFA whenever he can.

“Sometimes travel is organised on commercial (including low-cost) airlines and sometimes it is on private charter, depending on which is more efficient and cost-effective under the circumstances. FIFA pays travel costs.”

News.title: Energy suppliers ordered to pass on VAT cut to bills to customers this winter
News.content:
Energy suppliers ordered to pass on VAT cut to bills to customers this winter

EXCLUSIVE: Chancellor John Healey and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh have written to suppliers to ensure households get the benefit of the reduction from 5% VAT to zero on electricity bills

View 2 Images Households will see cut to VAT on electricity bills this winter (Image: Natalia Gdovskaia via Getty Images)

Energy suppliers have been ordered to pass on VAT cuts to electricity bills to all consumers this winter.

‌



Chancellor John Healey and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh have written to suppliers to ensure households get the benefit of the reduction from 5% VAT to zero on domestic bills.

‌



The move, one of Andy Burnham's first pledges as Prime Minister, will come into force on October 1.

‌



It is expected to knock about £45 off the annual bill for a typical household, as part of the new PM's efforts to give people a bit of breathing space on the cost of living.

Ms Fahnbulleh told The Mirror: "As Energy Secretary, I want to make one thing absolutely clear to Mirror readers: my focus is on bringing your energy bills down for good.

New PM Andy Burnham announces VAT cuts on household electricity bills from October READ MORE :

Andy Burnham to bring back £2 bus fare cap slashing travel costs for millions READ MORE :

View 2 Images Miatta Fahnbulleh and John Healey after Andy Burnham's first cabinet meeting in Downing Street (Image: Phil Lewis/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

‌



"That’s why on my first day in the job, we announced a cut to taxes on electricity bills, which will kick in from 1 October. And alongside the Chancellor, I've written to suppliers to make sure savings reach every customer, no matter what tariff they're on."

She acknowledged many families still feel their bills are too high despite the move to strip green levies from bills at the last Budget, which the then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves said would take £150 off energy bills.

Ms Fahnbulleh said: "This action is just the first step. This is a down payment to give households much-needed breathing space on the cost of living this winter.

‌



"But I am very clear there is much more to do. We will tackle the cost of living with greater public control to make life's essentials affordable again, and bring back hope."

Officials are working with the regulator Ofgem to ensure providers pass the saving on to consumers.

In a letter to suppliers, the Chancellor and the Energy Secretary said: "We are writing today to ask for your confirmation... that you will fully pass through the VAT reduction to all your domestic customers, including those on fixed tariffs, for the duration of the cut to reassure consumers across the country that they will feel these savings.

‌



"We are grateful for the work that you did with government to ensure that the Budget 2025 measures were fully passed on – and expect suppliers to do the same here so that we can collectively ensure that the full benefit is felt by consumers.

Downing Street said the new measure - estimated to cost £850 million in 2026-27 - will be funded by savings from the scrapped digital ID programme, which was going to cost £1.8bn over the next three years.

However the claim sparked a row as sacked Cabinet Minister Darren Jones, who led on the digital ID plan, said it had not been funded. He posted on X: “The Digital ID program was unfunded. The government will have to set out how it will pay for its new policies at the Budget.”

Article continues below

But Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said it was a "straightforward switch spend", redirecting money for digital ID. Departments had been working to find saving for the scheme, which will now be reallocated to pay for the VAT cut.

News.title: Four men in 20s killed in horror crash after car smashes into lamp-post in Huyton
News.content:
Four men in 20s killed in horror crash after car smashes into lamp-post in Huyton

Four men in their 20s have died after a car left the road and crashed into a lamp-post in Huyton, Merseyside, in the early hours of Friday, Merseyside Police said

Huge police presence in Huyton as four killed in crash

Four men in their 20s have been killed in a major crash which saw a car hit a lamp-post in Merseyside.

‌



Police were called to Liverpool Road in Huyton just before 2am this morning, July 24. It followed a report that a black Seat Cupra had come off the road after crashing into a lamp-post on the road, travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley.

‌



Emergency services attended, but two men aged 23 and two other men aged 24 and 26 were pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



Their next of kin have been informed are being supported by specially-trained officers.

A 27-year-old man who was a passenger inside the car has been taken to hospital where he remains in a stable condition, reports the Liverpool Echo.

View 3 Images Four men have died in the collision (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



Eleven roads in the area have been closed, including Liverpool Road and East Prescot Road - in both directions from its junction with Finch Lane to its junction with Princess Drive. The closures are likely to remain in place over the weekend.

Merseyside Police has asked anyone who may have witnessed the crash, or those with doorbell footage of the incident, to get in touch.

Superintendent Paul Holden said: "First and foremost our thoughts are with the family of the four men who sadly lost their lives following the collision in the early hours of this morning. Their families have been informed and are being supported by our specially trained family liaison officers.

‌



View 3 Images Police at the cordoned off Liverpool Road (Image: Liverpool Echo)

"This is a truly devastating moment for their families and loved ones, and it is now our priority to get answers for them on how the collision occurred.

"We know this happened very early this morning, but if anyone saw what happened or were driving through the area just before the incident occurred then please get in touch. Similarly, if you live in the area and have doorbell footage of the black Seat Cupra or the incident itself, please contact us.

‌



"You may have information or footage that would be useful to our investigation."

A temporary flight restriction zone - specifically affecting drones - is in place above Liverpool Road in Huyton under article 239 of the Air Navigation Order 2016.

This means drones are not permitted to fly within the area outlined by Merseyside Police.

‌



View 3 Images Drones are not permitted to fly in the area outlined (Image: Merseyside Police)

Drone users flying inside the Restricted Airspace that have not been granted permission will be guilty of committing an offence and could be prosecuted as well as having their equipment seized and confiscated.

Merseyside Police Drones, air ambulances, Fire Service Drones and NPAS are excluded from the airspace restriction.

Article continues below

Anyone who wishes to seek consideration for the safe and appropriate flight of a drone in these areas must obtain permission from Merseyside Police, Tac Ad on 07971688873.

Anyone with information about this collision is asked to DM @MerPolCC, contact the Serious Collision Investigation Unit on (0151) 777 5747, or email SCIU@merseyside.police.uk quoting reference number 26000600149.

News.title: 'Iran is threatening UK and looking for anyone to lash out at - it could get much worse'
News.content:
The UK has issued a robust response declaring it is ready to defend itself against Iranian threats over the American use of British bases to launch bombing runs against Tehran. It was inevitable that even though RAF Fairford is primarily used as a US air force base the distinction would be lost on the Iranians- after all it is called RAF Fairford in the UK. And the same goes for former Prime Minister Keir Starmer giving permission for the US to launch defensive actions from there, other UK bases and the island of Diego Garcia.

Iran will not see the difference between defensive and offensive and it needs a vulnerable junior US partner to target with no guarantee of harsh consequences. Normally this would mean the UK was giving permission to launch strikes against Iranian missile-firing capability in order to defend the region against attack. But, again, it was always likely that Iran would not appreciate the difference between offensive and defensive. Iran knows that US B1 bombers have taken off from there.

View 4 Images Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile launch (Image: SEPAHNEWS.COM/AFP via Getty Images)

And all of this comes as US President Donald Trump has warned he is deciding whether to escalate attacks on Iran this weekend, in a deeply alarming shift of tempo.

‌



One UK security source, with close connection to the US military machine, told the Daily Mirror on Friday: “There is increasing concern that Trump will escalate this weekend. It is very possible this may involve some kind of ground incursion. Both Trump and so-called Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had a terrible week because of the lack of mission clarity and strategy and there has been no shift in attitude form the Iranians.

“Trump may do it to distract from his various issues and Hegseth because he has a deranged sense of masculinity and is obsessed with displaying US military power. But taking the fight to Iran will not be popular.”

None of this will abate concerns about security in the UK. Given the Iranian threat that RAF Fairford is, according to Iran, now a “legitimate target” that means the military will boost protection of air bases.

View 4 Images Escalation: US President Donald Trump (Image: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

‌



This will involve troops from the RAF Regiment beefing up perimeter protection, patrols and looking for ‘hostile reconnaissance,” where potential attackers scope their targets. Anyone looking suspicious is likely to be questioned.

Iran has also issued a threat “warning to the British monarchy” which is also worrying and may lead to extra patrols by armed Royal Protection police. And exactly what the threat would be is vague, although Iran has recently started employing what the Israeli Mossad agency called a “proxy by proxy” approach.

This means employing at arms length criminal elements to do their dirty work, but perhaps several times removed, using groups loosely connected to Iranian intelligence. In the coming weeks and months it will become increasingly difficult for Britain to distance itself from the war in Iran since Tehran is looking for anyone to lash out at.

View 4 Images Precision US strikes on Iran's military (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The UK is seen as a junior partner to the US, regardless of the fact Starmer made it clear this country was not overtly going to become involved in the war.

It will also become increasingly difficult because Iran is looking for anyone to lash out at - witness its attacks on its neighbouring Gulf States. With war spreading to Iran’s Houthis in Yemen and Iran’s Iraqi proxies, both have entered the fight and are now claiming they are attacking the US in the Middle East. There is little hope for a quick solution. And depending on what Trump decides this weekend the situation is looking set to become much worse.

News.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana appears to be manipulating the system, families' lawyer says
News.content:
A lawyer for the families of the children murdered by Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has said his transfer from prison to a psychiatric hospital may be an attempt to "manipulate the system".

Rudakubana, 19, was given a life sentence for the murder of three children - Alice da Silva Aguiar, 9, Bebe King, 6, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, 7 - and attempted murder of eight other children and two adults.

On Thursday, he was moved from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Prisoners who are considered to present a risk to staff, inmates or themselves because of mental disorders can be moved to hospital under the Mental Health Act.

Next Wednesday marks two years since Rudakubana carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on 29 July 2024.

Lawyer Chris Walker, who represents the three bereaved families, said they "don't believe the merits" of the transfer on the basis of a mental health issue and is calling for more information from ministers.

"In my mind this is a new event, this is something which occurred whilst he was at prison, and we at this stage don't believe the merits of it in terms of him because I've seen no evidence at all until today which suggests he has a significant mental health disorder," Walker told BBC Radio 4's Today Programme.

"We do have an evil person but being evil does not mean that you're suffering with psychosis of some sort.

"We need to know is this a single event, is this a recurring event, is this him playing the system and we need those answers."

The Prison Officers' Association told the BBC that Rudakubana was transferred due to a deterioration in his mental health.

Walker added in a separate statement that the news would "devastate" the families at any time but "the fact that this has occurred as we approach the second anniversary in our view is another move by AR who would appear to be attempting, once again, to manipulate the system".

"We have been given the barest of details and whilst we are supporting the families through this we are urgently seeking a meeting with the appropriate authorities to understand the situation before commenting further."

Prior to Rudakubana's sentencing last year, his defence lawyer told the court no psychiatric evidence could suggest a mental disorder contributed to his actions.

Stan Reiz KC added that his client had appeared to have been a "normal child" until he reached 13.

"However, he did make a transition from a normal, well-disciplined child to someone who was capable of committing acts of such shocking and senseless violence."

Handing down the judgement, Justice Julian Goose said: "Many who have heard the evidence might describe what he did as evil, who could dispute it?"

He added: "I am sure Rudakubana had the settled determination to carry out these offences and had he been able to, he would have killed each and every child - all 26 of them."

The Southport Public Inquiry has heard evidence about his past mental health conditions.

Rudakubana was given a 52-year prison sentence in January 2025 but the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to Rudakubana being 17 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

In May 2025 there was an investigation after Rudakubana allegedly attacked a prison officer with boiling water.

Under the Mental Health Act, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) is likely to have had no choice but to accept doctors' recommendations about whether Rudakubana could be held safely in prison.

The law requires he be transferred back to prison when he no longer requires treatment in hospital. His sentence is not being converted into a "hospital order", which would mean he stayed at Broadmoor.

Confirming the transfer on Thursday, the MoJ said the families of those murdered and injured would be in the country's heart forever and "our thoughts remain with them" and said it does not change Rudakubana's sentence.

A statement continued: "Any decision to transfer an offender is made following an independent, clinical assessment, under the Mental Health Act.

"Following rigorous security checks, the offender has been transferred to a high-security psychiatric unit, where he will remain until assessed fit to return to prison."

News.title: 'Extremely significant' bomb in car intercepted on way to NI, Irish police say
News.content:

The vehicle was stopped during an operation targeting dissident republican activities on Wednesday but further details are just emerging. Two people were arrested.

The vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, at about 15:00 local time on Wednesday.

Irish broadcaster RTÃ has reported that gardaÃ­ (Irish police) sources said the bomb contained a power unit, a detonator and military grade explosives.

News.title: Angela Rayner rules out rent controls in England
News.content:
Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is not looking at bringing in rent controls in England.

She told BBC Breakfast that changes made through the Renters' Rights Act, which came into effect in May, were "already having a significant impact on the market".

She added that controls which had been implemented in some areas of the UK over the past few years had not "necessarily brought rents down".

In 2023 when he was the mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham called for freezes to private sector rents until the cost of living crisis was over.

But Rayner told the BBC on Friday: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment.

"Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market.

"We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

Temporary rent controls were introduced in Scotland in October 2022 but expired last year.

Under new legislation, ministers in Holyrood will be able to designate certain places in Scotland as rent control areas - expected to come in by 2027.

Councils will be able to cap rent increases on some properties at a maximum of 6%.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said he wants to see rent controls brought in for all rented property in England.

Responding to Rayner's interview, he described Burnham as "continuity Starmer", posting on X: "The new prime minister talks a lot of about helping with the cost of living crisis. This is the one single measure that would help the most and save billions. All talk."

Jeremy Corbyn, who pledged to bring in rent controls during the 2019 general election when he was the Labour leader, described Rayner's announcement as "extremely disappointing".

"There is no hope of ending homelessness if we do not stand up to vested interests and take action against extortionate private rents.

"We need rent controls, and we need them now."

Sir Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, has also long called on the government to implement a cap.

The term rent controls describes a range of measures a government can implement - from capping price increases to freezing them for a period of time.

Landlord groups say they may exacerbate the housing crisis by putting owners off renting out property.

The Renters' Rights Act was brought in to give more stability and security to the 11 million people who rent from private landlords.

Under the legislation, fixed-term tenancies have been banned and it is now significantly harder for landlords to evict tenants.

Rents can also only be increased once a year to the property's "open market rent".

News.title: Chris Mason: What Burnham's first week in power tells us about his agenda
News.content:
"We are on borrowed time if we don't get a move on," Angela Rayner, the former deputy prime minister who is back in the cabinet this week as housing secretary, told the BBC's Today programme on Friday.

It has been quite the week at Westminster. Sir Keir Starmer's departure as prime minister on Monday seems rather a while ago.

The fledgling Burnham administration has been seeking to find its feet and make a decent first impression at the same time, as many try to do in the first days in a job.

There has been an early pattern in these early days: an early morning nugget of news dropping from No10.

On Thursday, it was business rates in England; on Wednesday, it was bus fares in England and on Tuesday, it was a VAT cut on electricity bills.

Today, the prime minister is assembling what Rayner calls "a pride of mayors" among others for a meeting of what is known as the National Economic Council at the new No10 North in Manchester.

Andy Burnham claims his new base in Manchester represents the beginning of "the biggest rebalancing of power our country has seen, external" and he will be "bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years".

His early announcements have been considerably more piecemeal than that â he says his "10 year plan for Britain" will come later in the year.

It is worth remembering there was talk from both Boris Johnson and his allies and from Sir Keir Starmer about their plans for the decade ahead â both fizzled out rather more quickly than that.

So how should we assess how much politics has changed, or not?

The early evidence - and let's be frank, it is only that given we are just a few days in - points to Andy Burnham being both more sharp and more nimble than his predecessor in setting out what he is attempting to do and trying to point to early examples of what that might look like, with the announcements of the last few days.

With the tinkering of how the government is run, like the creation of the Office of Prime Minister, and the establishment of No 10 North, he's made it clear that the arteries of power flow very much to and from him.

He hopes he can overcome the critique of Sir Keir Starmer and others, that one of the frustrations of being prime minister can be pulling levers and nothing actually happens.

News.title: Chris Brown pleads guilty to affray over nightclub attack in London
News.content:
The attack happened at the Tape venue, a private members' club in Mayfair, on 19 February 2023.

Brown entered his plea at Southwark Crown Court on Friday in a hearing that took less than five minutes.

Judge Tony Baumgartner scheduled the sentencing hearing for the affray charges for both men for 26 October, 2026.

Brown is known for tracks including Loyal, Look At Me Now and With You.

He waved at fans as he arrived at court, flanked by security guards while wearing a beige suit and baseball cap.

Fans played Brown's music, held up signs and shouted his name, with the PA news agency reporting that one said: "I love you Chris".

At earlier hearings, he was ordered to pay a Â£5m security fee as part of his bail conditions, which also allowed him to go on a world tour as long as he surrendered his passport on arrival in each country.

Last summer, the performer joked on-stage about his "nice" time in jail in Manchester as he kicked off his tour at the city's Co-Op Live arena.

"Thank you for coming and supporting me," he said to fans in Manchester. "And thank you to the jail," he joked, referring to a spell in custody after his arrest. "It was really nice."

News.title: They became best friends - then discovered they were brother and sister
News.content:
Dave Green and Andrea Urmston found they instantly hit it off when their paths crossed while working in separate roles at Manchester Airport.

The two strangers got on so well they could complete each other's sentences - which made sense when they discovered the truth.

Dave was Andrea's biological brother, but had been adopted by another family when he was a baby.

"I was shaking, I was just shaking and my heart was pounding," Andrea told the BBC. "I'd finally found him. It's unbelievable."

In 2005, Dave was managing the bus station at the airport and Andrea serviced the vending machines.

Over the next two years they became firm friends, texting and phoning each other when they were not at work.

One day during a phone call, Dave told Andrea something he had never mentioned before. He was adopted and his birth name was Stuart Proudlove.

"I kind of froze and didn't speak for a minute," said Andrea.

Her maiden name was Proudlove and she had a brother who was adopted before she was born.

"It's not a very popular name and it had to be him. Other than family, I had never heard that surname anywhere else," she added.

She immediately rang her mother, Susan, to check her long-lost brother's birth date. They matched: 24 March 1966. She called Dave straight back.

"I said 'it's got to be you, it's got to be you', and I said 'I need to see you', and so I went to pick him up," Andrea said.

News.title: Fifty women tell BBC they were pressured into having sex with strangers
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual acts

Fifty women have told the BBC they were pressured or coerced by their partners into having sex with strangers.

They got in contact following an investigation which told the story of a woman who said she had been pressured into having sex with more than 100 people she did not know.

Many of the women who came forward said they had sex through swinging despite not wanting to, either because they feared the consequences of refusing or felt they had to keep their partners happy.

They spoke of deep, long-lasting trauma.

"I remember many nights of my partner keeping me up all night screaming at me, threatening me, and attempting to gaslight me into believing this was something I wanted," said one woman. "It was never what I wanted."

Another told us: "I felt like I had been given away. I felt used. I felt so dirty."

Most encounters were arranged via the website FabSwingers, say the women, which claims to have more than half a million UK active monthly accounts.

Six women told BBC News they had been raped by men met through the site.

One said her partner had forced her to have sex with more than 90 men through FabSwingers. On one occasion, he held her down by the ankles, she told us.

Sixteen said intimate photos of them had been uploaded to the website without their permission.

News.title: Firefighting helicopter brought in to tackle Isle of Wight blaze
News.content:
A helicopter has been brought in as firefighters continue to fight a large heathland blaze on the Isle of Wight.

The gorse fire was first reported at Headon Warren, in the West Wight, shortly after 09:00 BST on Thursday, and is affecting a 25-hectare (62-acre) area of woodland.

Crews from Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service worked overnight to extinguish the blaze using jets and hose reels and have arranged for a helicopter water-drop to reach inaccessible areas.

Additional fire appliances have been taken to the island to support the efforts to fight the fire which is on land owned by the National Trust. The public has been told to stay away.

News.title: Hero swimmer helped two children during beach tragedy
News.content:
Witnesses say a heroic day-tripper managed to haul two children back to shore during an incident where a mother and daughter drowned.

Beverly Smit, 60, described the unnamed rescuer swimming out to sea three times as the tragedy unfolded in West Mersea, near Colchester, on Wednesday evening.

Shally Rahman, 41, and Samiha Rahman, 15, were trying to rescue a seven-year-old boy from the water when they got into difficulty and died.

Essex Police said the group, from Barking, east London, were all related to each other and the boy remained in hospital, fighting for his life.

Recalling the moment the "Good Samaritan" sprang into action, Smit said: "They were calling for help and the children and adults were out there.

"He swam out, I think, three times. Two of the children he brought back were not in good condition.

"It's not an easy swim when the tide's coming in - you're swimming against the tide. The water [on Wednesday] was particularly quite cold."

News.title: Novel analysis reveals playful side of Alan Turing
News.content:
A story written by World War Two codebreaker Alan Turing suggests he was a man with playful humour embracing his homosexuality, according to new analysis.

The six-page hand-written short story, Pryce's Buoy, has been transcribed in full for the first time and studied by Sarah Dillon, professor of literature at the University of Cambridge.

Dillon said the story offered fresh insights that challenge the view of Turing as an isolated, lonely genius.

"We've distilled a version of Turing that is a two-dimensional stereotype," she added.

Turing played a crucial role in the Allies' victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two by helping to crack codes and deciphering the infamous Enigma machine at Bletchley Park.

After the war he produced a detailed design for a digital computer in the modern sense, storing programmes in its memory.

News.title: UK mortgage rates rise to highest level for a month
News.content:
UK average mortgage rates have risen back to the level of a month ago as renewed tensions in the Middle East feed through to homeowners.

Lenders' funding costs have increased as markets judge that a prolonged conflict reduces the possibility of interest rate cuts by central banks.

The five biggest High Street banks are among a host of lenders which have increased their interest rates on new fixed deals in recent days.

Recent projections by the Bank of England suggest just over five million homeowners should expect their monthly mortgage repayments to increase by the end of 2028.

Mortgage rates had been falling as a ceasefire between the US and Iran initially appeared to hold.

But fresh strikes and Houthi militia attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea reignited fears over global energy supplies.

Oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May on Thursday after several days of increases, stoking fears of higher inflation and a lower likelihood of interest rate cuts.

News.title: Man who paid for children to be sexually abused jailed
News.content:
A 76-year-old man who paid for children in the Philippines to be sexually abused to order has been jailed.

Robert Pasteiner, from Chichester, West Sussex, was identified through suspicious payments totalling more than Â£200,000 made to individuals in the South East Asian country, including arrested facilitators of live-streamed child sexual abuse.

He was arrested at Heathrow Airport in 2023 before he was due to fly to the Philippines.

Pasteiner was sentenced at Portsmouth Crown Court to 12 years in prison after pleading guilty to 36 offences.

Mobile phone analysis discovered that he had arranged to meet a 12-year-old girl in his hotel in the Philippines.

A search of his luggage found condoms and Viagra, as well as presents.

Further searches of his home uncovered 15 electronic devices, six of which contained indecent images of children.

Paperwork seized contained payment details, how much money had been sent and what the payments were for â noting some as being for a "show".

Pasteiner pleaded guilty to causing or inciting the sexual exploitation of a child, attempted sexual communication with a child, arranging or facilitating the sexual exploitation of a child and making indecent images of children.

He also received a Sexual Harm Prevention Order and will be on the Sex Offender's Register for life.

The National Crime Agency (NCA) said it worked with the National Bureau of Investigation and Philippine National Police to identify and safeguard his victims.

Senior investigating officer Danielle Pownall said: "Robert Pasteiner is a depraved man who posed a significant threat to children around the world.

"The items recovered during our investigation are a clear sign of his intentions in travelling to the Philippines."

News.title: Wildfire spotted from space as helicopter brought in to tackle blaze
News.content:
Satellite images have captured plumes of smoke and the damage caused by a wildfire in north Wales.

Data gathered by BBC Verify suggests an estimated 951 hectares (2,350 acres) of the Rhinogydd mountains in Gwynedd have been devastated by a wildfire that broke out earlier this month.

Nasa's satellite-based fire monitoring system has also detected heat signatures from four areas of Wales where wildfires have recently occurred.

It is also showing heat sources at Blaenavon in Torfaen, Presteigne in Powys, and Pentre Halkyn in Flintshire.

News.title: Heat health alerts in effect for parts of UK as rain returns for some this weekend
News.content:
Yellow heat health alerts came into effect across central and southern England on Friday morning with temperatures forecast to reach 30C (86F) in places.

The alerts, issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), cover the East and West Midlands, eastern England, London, south-east England and south-west England and are valid from 09:00 BST on Friday until 09:00 on Sunday.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

It comes as parts of the UK prepare to see much-needed rain this weekend - although amounts are expected to be relatively small, especially in the south.

A drought was officially declared for large parts of north and mid-Wales on Thursday.

The rest of Wales, along with much of central, southern and eastern England, is in "prolonged dry weather" category - one stage below a drought - and the Sottish Environment Protection Agency said much of eastern Scotland has moved into 'water scarcity' status

Hosepipe bans are in force for millions of the customers across eastern and southern England.

News.title: King's Tardis entrance as Commonwealth Games begin
News.content:
One of the louder cheers came for the Falklands Islands â in the news recently following Argentina's victory over England in the football World Cup semi-finals â and another followed when the Samoa team emerged and performed a haka in front of the dignitaries in the Royal Box.

But nothing compared to the noise which greeted the arrival of the Scotland team, who entered the arena last in their white shirts and kilts and lifted many in the capacity crowd from their seats.

A large Loch Ness Monster representation then emerged, before, backed by bagpipers and drummers, a rousing rendition of Flower of Scotland followed.

The next section of the evening featured theatrical performances â a show billed as "a love letter to Glasgow and the Commonwealth".

It began with a performance by Scottish folk and country singer Nathan Evans and a dance under a replica of Glasgow Central Station's iconic clock.

The saying "Meet me under the clock" is famous in these parts.

Singer Callum Beattie's rendition of Baccara's Yes Sir, I Can Boogie â the 1970s disco tune recently adopted as Scotland's unofficial anthem - had the Scottish athletes dancing in their seats.

Held indoors in front of about 10,000 people, this was a more intimate ceremony than the last time Glasgow hosted the Commonwealth Games, when a 40,000-strong crowd witnessed the opening of the Games in 2014 at Celtic Park.

There was a point, after the Australian state of Victoria withdrew as hosts in 2023, when some thought these Games would not happen. Glasgow stepped in at short notice to ensure otherwise.

There are eight fewer sports involved compared to 2014, given the short build-up, and venues from 12 years ago have been repurposed.

But Commonwealth Sport president Donald Rukare, wearing a tartan kilt in the colours of his home country Uganda, said this edition has been made possible by the "extraordinary legacy of 2014 and by a city that once again welcomes us with warm hearts and open arms".

Iran has trolled U.S. secretary of state Marco Rubio after he hit out at the “stupid Lego videos” that have spoofed the war on social media.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Rubio acknowledged the viral clips – while he insisting he had never seen them – when he was asked about the current state of negotiations with Iran.

“They’re probably not ready to do a deal yet, but they will be soon because the price they’re paying is very high despite their tough talk and their flowery language and their stupid Lego videos they put out – I’ve never seen them, but they put these things out on social media,” he said.

“Despite all that bravado, they are suffering tremendously, and they’re going to suffer more until they come to their senses.”

open image in gallery Explosive Media posted the new Lego clip shortly after Marco Rubio called the videos “stupid” ( X/ExplosiveMediaa )

The comments were soon followed by an A.I. generated clip mocking ‘Little Marco’, shared on X by the Explosive Media account that has produced previous similar videos.

Set to a spoof rap, a Lego Rubio is branded “a little lapdog stuck under the loser’s thumb” in reference to President Donald Trump who appears in the clip yelling at him.

“No mercy! Little Marco, this one is for you. Bricks, Beats, Total destruction,” read a caption alongside the clip.

The video shows Rubio in a bath and with a cape on top of a building like a superhero. It references multiple real-life Iranian attacks on the U.S. and mocks: “Were they made out of Lego?”

At one point in the footage shows the Rubio character having to use a stool to reach a light switch and wearing clown make up.

The caption describes the clip as ‘a message from Zolfaghari’, presumably referring to the Iranian military officer of the same name.

Earlier, the Iranian commentator and professor Seyed Mohammad Marandi reposted the clip of Rubio’s original interview on X, adding: “The Lego guys have made the angry little man even angrier.”

Iran has released a series of Lego videos mocking American politicians that have accrued millions of views online since the war began at the end of February.

A spokesperson for Explosive Media previously denied working for the Iranian government in an interview with the BBC in April, but described the regime as “a customer”.

open image in gallery Rubio said he had never seen the clips but that described them as ‘stupid’ ( Reuters )

The White House has posted its own share of trolling videos too, with a number of clips in the early days of the war making reference to video games like Grand Theft Auto and Call of Duty.

Rubio’s latest comments on the state of the war come after nearly a fortnight of strikes by the U.S., launched after the fragile ceasefire collapsed.

Iran and the U.S. have both insisted they currently have the upper hand, with reports Trump is considering launching a ‘major attack’ on Tehran following recent strikes on tankers in the Gulf.

However, U.S. intelligence assessments earlier this week suggested the Trump administration had been told ongoing strikes on Iran would not influence the Islamic Republic’s negotiating position or change its demands.

open image in gallery The spoof videos have been part of the online propaganda war between the U.S. and Iran ( Explosive Media )

The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that Trump is now in “revenge mode” after growing increasingly frustrated over the stalemate and believes Iran only understands force, according to allies.

The journal said the U.S. was sending forces, medics and weaponry to the region to give more options if Washington chooses to escalate again.

Meanwhile the number of tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz fell to just one on Thursday, the lowest level since 7 May. The large carrier New Giant, loaded with 2 million barrels of Iraqi Basrah crude, exited the strait and is due to arrive at China's Rizhao port by mid-August.

News.title: Paper checks should have disappeared by now. So why are billions still being written in the US?
News.content:
