Volpato was born and raised in Sydney and played junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers before moving overseas to join Serie A club Roma.

He left Roma after two seasons to join Sassuolo where he has scored seven goals in three seasons, before making his mark with the Socceroos and shaping up as a key to the national side’s future.

Sports.title: Chelsea paid Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers. Is he the right fit?
Sports.content:
It quickly became apparent this summer that Aston Villa would not be holding on to Morgan Rogers. Having helped the club finish fourth in the Premier League and win the Europa League, the 23-year-old was in demand.

Arsenal looked like his likeliest next destination, with the champions eager to strengthen the left side of their attack. The charm offensive came from many angles, with Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Arteta and the club’s England players trying to sell the idea to Rogers. But, with Arsenal reluctant to meet Villa’s asking price, Chelsea intervened and made Rogers the most expensive British player ever, surpassing the £116m that Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer.

Xabi Alonso is new to Chelsea, so it is difficult to know exactly where Rogers will play. The versatile forward, who started out at West Brom before moving to Manchester City, Middlesbrough and then Villa, will probably be used in a variety of roles – often starting from the left but having opportunities to take up various attacking positions.

Alonso predominantly used a 3-4-3 formation at Bayer Leverkusen and a 4-2-3-1 at Real Madrid. If Chelsea play with three at the back, Rogers will be the left-sided No 10 in the team; if they use a four-man defence, he will start slightly wider but with the freedom to come inside – or he might even occupy the central role.

If Alonso goes with the style he used at Leverkusen, Rogers might not be the best fit. During Alonso’s two full seasons in the Bundesliga, the team averaged 62.1% (2023-24) and 59.6% (2024-25) possession. During their title-winning campaign in 2023-24, they went unbeaten all season while dominating the ball and moving up the pitch slowly.

They were set up to patiently build with lots of passes, win back possession quickly if they lost it and keep the ball as close to the opposition’s goal as possible. They made 367 high turnovers, which was 54 more than any other side. This system works best with attacking players who are tidy and intricate in tight spaces. However, Rogers is at his most effective when he can use his pace and gallop into space.

His dribble completion rate last season was 34.2%, which was nothing to shout about. And his completion rate for passes under pressure was 73.4% – again not exceptional. Of the 161 forwards and midfielders who attempted at least 300 passes under pressure last season, Rogers ranked 143rd. The statistics suggest he is not particularly effective in close-quarters engagements.

With space to attack, Rogers is a threat. He made 223 progressive carries last season, the 10th highest among Premier League forwards, wingers and attacking midfielders. Only Cody Gakpo (41) and Matheus Cunha (35) had more carries that ended in shots than Rogers (30). He also created 16 chances for teammates after a carry: only 11 players created more. Rogers’ combined 46 chances created and shots taken following carries put him behind just Jérémy Doku (58), Gakpo (57) and Bukayo Saka (56). Alonso’s passing style may not bring the best from Rogers.

There are reasons for optimism though. Rogers is frequently on the move and that makes him difficult to track. Only four players made more off-ball runs in the league last season; his 160 off-ball runs ending in the box was the eighth highest in the division.

View image in fullscreen A mural of Jude Bellingham and Rogers in Birmingham. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian

He also has the potential to form a good relationship with João Pedro. The Brazilian will probably be the focal point of the team and he is not a conventional No 9. He likes to drop deep, link with teammates and be a creator almost as much as a finisher. With Pedro dropping back, there will be room for Rogers to exploit beyond him: he made 258 runs in behind last season, the 12th highest in the league.

Rogers’ strong relationship with Ollie Watkins bodes well for Chelsea. He created 20 open-play chances for Watkins last season, which was the second most from one player to another in the league. Wherever he has played, Rogers has developed an understanding with his teammates. He already has a close friendship with Cole Palmer after their time together in the Manchester City academy.

Rogers’ other great attribute is his ball-striking ability. Since he made his Premier League debut in February 2024, Rogers has scored 21 non-penalty goals from 14.7 non-penalty expected goals. His overperformance of +6.3 is the 10th highest in the league.

Rogers has a great strike on him and it could be a gamechanger for Chelsea, particularly when they play teams employing a low block. His five league goals from outside the box since his Villa debut is bettered by only six players. Few players are as accurate when shooting from distance. It was his shot against Norway that led to Jude Bellingham’s winning goal in the World Cup quarter-final.

Chelsea have paid an incredible amount of money for Rogers and there are reasons to wonder if the move will work tactically. But Rogers has a habit of making an impact regardless of the context. He’s not a right winger but he still made his presence known for England against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, setting up Anthony Gordon’s opener from the right.

Is he a £117m player? Perhaps not. Will he succeed playing the same way he played at Villa? Perhaps not. But it’s hard to imagine him not making a significant impact at Stamford Bridge.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: David Beckham and Ronaldo are competing at the Commonwealth Games... but not THOSE ones! Indian cyclists - named after football legends - are going for gold in Glasgow
Sports.content:
David Beckham and Ronaldo are competing at the Commonwealth Games... but not THOSE ones! Indian cyclists - named after football legends - are going for gold in Glasgow

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A pair of Indian cyclists named after football legends David Beckham and Ronaldo will catch the eye when they take to the velodrome at the Commonwealth Games next week.

David Beckham Elkatohchoongo and Ronaldo Laitonjam Singh have dominated the Indian cycling scene and will hope to create their own legacies by winning gold at the Games in Glasgow.

Sports fans may be bemused when they see the pair's names on the timesheets at the Sir Chris Hoy velodrome, having hailed from football-mad families.

'My [uncle] is a big fan of David Beckham's,' Beckham Elkatohchoongot, 23, told Times of India in 2020.

'I have never seen a mad fan like him. In 2002 they celebrated and danced all night when Beckham scored the goal [against Argentina at the World Cup] and took his team to a win.

'I was born in 2003 and he fought with my mother and my [grandfather] to give me the name 'David Beckham.' That's how I got the name.'

An Indian cyclist named David Beckham will be going for gold at the Commonwealth Games

He is named after England legend Golden Balls, while his Indian team-mate Ronaldo is named after football icon Ronaldinho (left)

Beckham Elkatohchoongo crashed out at the 2022 Commonwealth Games but there is genuine hope that he will win gold this time around.

Ronaldo, 24, is named after Brazil and Barcelona legend Ronaldinho, rather than Ronaldo Nazario or Cristiano Ronaldo.

The day before he was born, Ronaldinho famously lobbed England goalkeeper David Seaman to send the Three Lions home from the 2002 World Cup.

His father made a bet that the Brazilian's free kick would go in and, as the ball went into the back of the net, his phone rang with news of his wife going into labour.

'Just as the ball went in the goal, I must have started making an appearance,' the cyclist told The Hindu.

'I think my dad won some money that day. That's probably why I got that name. He felt I was very lucky for him.'

Beckham will compete in the men's Keirin while Ronaldo is in the men's 1000m time trial.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp confirmed as Germany manager - and has already threatened to QUIT after World Cup's 'most controversial WAG' was criticised: 'If you don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone'
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp confirmed as Germany manager - and has already threatened to QUIT after World Cup's 'most controversial WAG' was criticised: 'If you don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jurgen Klopp has been unveiled as Germany manager – and has already revealed what will make him quit the job.

The Liverpool legend, 59, is back in the dugout having enjoyed a stint overseeing Red Bull's football operation after leaving Anfield in 2024, and has been tasked with turning the national team around after another disappointing major tournament.

Julian Nagelsmann was given his marching orders after the Germans crashed out to Paraguay in the Round of 32, leading to an inquest into the team's performance –where the players' WAGs and families were placed under the spotlight.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

But Klopp has already set his stall in a robust unveiling, insisting that he will quit the job immediately if his family face any scrutiny.

'The day you don't want me anymore, you say so and I'm gone, without severance pay,' he said via Bild.

'If you say tomorrow that he's rubbish, I'm gone. Not just one person, it would have to be more than that. If the DFB says he's rubbish, I'm gone. If you behave badly and don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone.'

Jurgen Klopp is Germany's new manager, but has already set out what will make him quit

Klopp says he will leave if the media 'don't leave my family in peace' after his predecessor Julian Nagelsmann's relationship with an ex-reporter made headlines

Klopp also described his appointment to the national team position as 'the highlight of my career'.

'Criticise me if something doesn't work. I'm happy to work on it. It's all about the job. Jurgen Klopp doesn't have a career after the national team. Ideally, this is the highlight of my career.'

Wurzenberger, 34, reportedly caused 'quite a stir' among the squad after being 'more present than probably any national team's coach before her'.

She was first spotted at Germany's pre-tournament camp in Frankfurt, when she was pictured watching training from a balcony along with a host of the players' partners.

And after her boyfriend's side thumped Curacao 7-1 - Wurzenberger hung around to watch the German substitutes complete their warm down.

It was then reported that she accompanied Nagelsmann back to the team hotel, before the duo were seen cycling to training together the following morning.

'There is naturally always that feeling that when the boss's wife is in the room, you might not always be completely honest at the table when talking about the national coach,' local reporters speculated during the tournament.

Klopp met second wife Ulla Sandrock in 2005 and married her that same year

Wurzenberger, and indeed Nagelsmann, also incited criticism from Germany legend Lothar Matthaus, who admitted her constant presence is far from 'ideal'.

The midfielder, who earned 150 caps, said on German television: 'She just shouldn't appear in the pictures too often - that wouldn't be ideal in my opinion.

'The players have days off and their families can come to the hotel. Lena (Wurzenberger) did that too. From my perspective, I think it's perfectly normal.

'Lena was able to come to the hotel just like the players' girlfriends and wives. You can see the solidarity - but the rule shouldn't apply to the coach. It has to happen during the time when we players are seeing their families.'

Nagelsmann and Wurzenberger are reported to have started dating soon after he split from his ex-wife Verena, following 15 years together, in 2022.

At that point Nagelsmann was manager of German giants Bayern Munich - and his new love interest reported on the club for Bild.

An article from the publication announcing their romance read: 'Julian Nagelsmann loves Bild reporter'.

Klopp married social worker and children's writer Ulla Sandrock in December 2005, having met at a pub during an Oktoberfest celebration that same year. He was previously married to ex-wife Sabine, with whom he shares a child.

Elsewhere, Arsenal legend Per Mertesacker will play an integral role in Klopp's transformation of the German national team, having been appointed the new Managing Director of Sport for the federation.

Sports.title: Daily Mail's Whistleblowers shortlisted for Best Sport Podcast at prestigious British Podcast Awards
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail's hit podcast Whistleblowers has been shortlisted for Best Sport Podcast at the prestigious British Podcast Awards.

The show, hosted by former Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg, broadcaster Gordon Smart and Daily Mail Football Editor Ian Ladyman, has been nominated alongside Gary Neville's Stick to Football and That Peter Crouch Podcast.

The nomination continues the Daily Mail's prominence in the world of podcasting, with investigative podcast Pipeline: Left to Die recently taking home Investigative Podcast of the Year at the News Podcast Awards.

The Daily Mail's hit podcast Whistleblowers has been shortlisted for Best Sport Podcast at the prestigious British Podcast Awards

The show is hosted by former Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg, broadcaster Gordon Smart and Daily Mail Football Editor Ian Ladyman

Every week, Mark, Gordon and Ian turn a wry eye on the beautiful game, drawing on their unique vantage points from inside the referee's room and the press box

Every week, Mark, Gordon and Ian turn a wry eye on the beautiful game, drawing on their unique vantage points from inside the referee's room and the press box.

From analysing the biggest VAR calls to player transfer PR disasters, the Whistleblowers team give audiences a sense of football from the inside, with a lot of laughs along the way.

Whistleblowers delivered three episodes a week throughout this summer's World Cup, keeping listeners across every twist of the tournament as it happened.

The hosts are joined by a revolving door of special guests, including some of the Mail's best-in-class football reporters, former professionals and internet personalities.

Some big names from last season included former Arsenal defender Lee Dixon, firebrand tennis star Nick Kyrgios and the Daily Mail’s own Craig Hope.

Winners of the award will be revealed at the awards ceremony on Thursday, 1 October, at indigo at The O2 in London.

Listen to Whistleblowers on Apple and Spotify, or watch the show on YouTube. New episodes are released every Tuesday and Thursday.

Sports.title: Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog reveals betting line opened just moments after US striker was sent off at the World Cup
Sports.content:
A gambling watchdog group has flagged the United States' Round-of-16 loss to Belgium as one of seven World Cup matches that may have drawn irregular betting activity during the tournament.

Specifically, the independent Group of Copenhagen cited a predictions market line titled 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?' as one potential issue, sources told The Athletic.

That line opened on July 2 shortly after Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. On July 5, after President Donald Trump urged FIFA to rescind Balogun's red card, the governing body opted instead to suspend his one-game ban until after the tournament, thereby allowing him to play in the loss to Belgium.

Curiously, the Group of Copenhagen's report specified that no other similar markets opened for the 14 other players who got a red card during the tournament, according to The Athletic. Now the group has requested an official explanation from FIFA on the Balogun case.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from both FIFA and Polymarket, neither of which have been accused of any misconduct in this case.

Operating under the Council of Europe's Macolin Convention of 2014, the Group of Copenhagen is an independent network that detects and prevents the manipulation of sports competitions around the world. For the 2026 World Cup, the organization reviewed all 104 matches from the tournament, which attracted more than $240 billion bets worldwide, according to the Group of Copenhagen.

A gambling watchdog has opened an investigation into Balogun's red card overhaul

Folarin Balogun (20) fouls Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic (4), resulting in a red card

Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia

Although its full report has not yet been published, a summary of its conclusions has been shared by the Council of Europe.

The US loss to Belgium was among seven 'yellow notices' raised by the Group of Copenhagen, which has two higher levels of concern: orange and red.

'The Group of Copenhagen's notices can be explained by atypical behaviors such as changes in odds or hedging liquidities, there are many explanations that are not manipulations,' Christian Kalb, a gambling industry expert who previously worked with the Group of Copenhagen, told The Athletic.

'The major problem is when there may be a conflict of interest and potential inside information on those issues,' she continued. 'When we speak of prediction markets, we can detect some unusual behaviors but we must be very careful as they can be used for hedging markets.

The Norwegian FA is planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Meanwhile, the Norwegian FA plans to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Trump's interference in Balogun's red card ban.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, adding that FIFA President Gianni Infantino made a 'great decision.'

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the sport, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness now says she is planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee.

'When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behavior and the organization's behavior, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Jude Bellingham's brutal dig at World Cup referee as unseen footage goes viral - moments before England star slapped Argentina rival following semi-final defeat
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed.

The Real Madrid star made a point of confronting Ismail Elfath – Lionel Messi's favourite referee – to share his grievances after England's 2-1 loss last week.

Argentina employed roughhouse tactics against England, committing 15 fouls, to book their place in the final against Spain, where they lost 1-0.

Leandro Paredes and Enzo Fernandez were seen as particularly dirty in the opening exchanges of the match.

Both teams came into the match with a heightened sense of rivalry after the South American side's declarations throughout the tournament that the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina.

Fresh footage from the referee's camera has been released by FIFA and in it, Bellingham is seen saying to the referee: 'Some shocking ones there, but all the best.'

Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed

He was annoyed at decisions that had gone in Argentina's favour in their tense encounter

Bellingham, who scored seven goals for the Three Lions at the tournament, later slapped Argentina rival Valentin Barco on the back of the head as scenes turned ugly in Atlanta.

In the build-up to the flashpoint, Spurs captain and Argentina defender Cristian Romero was seen goading Bellingham when the final whistle was blown.

He went over to Barco and slapped him on the back of the head.

The full-back then turned around and pushed Bellingham with tempers flaring. Nicolas Otamendi also came over and gave the England man a shove.

Several Argentine players attempted to act as peacemakers, but it looked as if Bellingham and Otamendi wanted more head-to-head action – even when they were separated.

During the celebrations Argentina's stars held aloft a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

Despite FIFA's ban on political flags, Romero, Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and ex-Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso celebrated with the controversial sign after the final whistle.

Captain and star player Lionel Messi was also seen dancing alongside the banner.

Bellingham was goaded by Argentina star Cristian Romero at the final whistle

The midfielder also clashed with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco after the semi-final

Bellingham appeared to slap new Chelsea man Barco on the back of the head

He was also at loggerheads with defender Nicolas Otamendi as other players tried to stop them

FIFA are already looking into disciplinary action relating to the banner and Argentina's behaviour following their loss to Spain in the final.

The South American side's dirty tactics against England, plus the consistent allegations throughout the tournament that things were 'rigged' in their favour, have not done Messi's popularity any favours on these shores.

Messi is now viewed unfavourably among almost half of the participants surveyed by YouGov.

After losing 1-0 to Spain some of the Argentina squad started fights with the Spanish players. Fernandez was sent off in normal time and Paredes was lambasted for attacking Eric Garcia and Gavi after the match.

Even Messi was dragged into their pathetic antics in the final, attempting to get Marc Cucurella sent off for briefly putting his hand over his mouth.

Messi also clashed with Bellingham in the semi-finals, though England fans have to admit that the legend was brilliant towards the end of the match, setting up both of his country's goals.

All of this has had a deleterious effect on Messi's popularity.

Coming into the World Cup, he was viewed favourably by 55 per cent of the public and unfavourably by just nine per cent.

Now, he is seen favourably by only 29 per cent and unfavourably by 44 per cent.

That means that, according to YouGov's poll, Messi's net favourability rating among Britons has fallen from +46 to -15. In short, people don't like him very much.

His score is far worse than his arch-rival Cristiano Ronaldo, whose net rating is -2.

And he certainly lost his stock with Daily Mail Sport's veteran columnist Jeff Powell, who bunged Messi out of his top five all-time players for his antics.

Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Ousmane Diomande, Nottingham Forest's £35m 'coup': Barred from training with Viktor Gyokeres after too many bust-ups, how he muzzled Erling Haaland and why he's the perfect fit for Oliver Glasner and the Premier League
Sports.content:
THE ANALYST - Ousmane Diomande, Nottingham Forest's £35m 'coup': Barred from training with Viktor Gyokeres after too many bust-ups, how he muzzled Erling Haaland and why he's the perfect fit for Oliver Glasner and the Premier League

Read THE ANALYST only on DailyMail+ to get the ultimate lowdown on the world's biggest talents - and tell you how they would fit in at YOUR club

Such is Ousmane Diomande's competitive nature that former Sporting Lisbon manager Ruben Amorim was frequently forced to intervene to stop him and Viktor Gyokeres coming to blows.

So much so, the pair were eventually prevented from playing against each other in training because the threat of a crunching challenge or tensions flaring up was too high. Diomande and the now Arsenal striker had several rows and physical battles on the training pitch. Small-sided games, in particular, became too risky. With the Ivorian centre back set to join Nottingham Forest in a deal worth around £35million, he will get another crack at his former team-mate.

Their rivalry was not born from animosity, rather a perfectionist drive – training, competitive matches or even a kick about in the garden were all treated the same.

That hyper-competitive spirit should see Diomande settle into life at Forest and the Premier League well and impress new manager Oliver Glasner – who once, speaking in a Crystal Palace press conference, admitted that winning is paramount, regardless of whether he was playing with his children or in a major final. They are cut from the same cloth.

Glasner had chased Diomande’s signature at Palace, targeting him as Marc Guehi’s replacement in January. But Palace did not move quickly enough and Diomande signed a new contract until 2030, featuring a prohibitive £68.5m release clause. But now, in his new job, the Austrian has got his man.

The fee represents exceptional value for Forest as they pivot to a back three having played a back four last season. They are getting a player familiar with Glasner's preferred 3-4-2-1, having enjoyed success in that shape under Amorim at Sporting.

Nottingham Forest are understood to be offering £32million for Ivory Coast centre back Ousmane Diomande

Diomande (left) and Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres (centre) were not even allowed to play against each other in training at Sporting Lisbon, such was the ferocity of their rivalry

The 22-year-old joined Sporting Lisbon three years ago from Danish side Midtjylland

Diomande has all the attributes of a defender capable of thriving in the Premier League. Not only is he fast and proficient on the ball but he thrives defensively thanks to his physical strength and solid 6ft 3in build.

In last season’s Champions League, he won 66 per cent of his duels and is a relentless battler. He does not make it easy for attackers. Erling Haaland learned the hard way in a Champions League group stage match two seasons ago, after Diomande marshalled him well throughout as Sporting thrashed Manchester City 4-1 in Lisbon.

His sprint speed will also be a valuable asset. Diomande possesses explosive recovery pace which will help Forest when defending with a high line. His ability to recover quickly will allow Forest to react more effectively when opponents look to exploit the space in behind during transitions. Glasner's Palace side often relied on it with Maxence Lacroix; Forest are likely to be no different with Diomande.

He will feature on the right of Forest’s back three, partnering Murillo and Nikola Milenkovic, as an imposing centre back. In Glasner’s system, he will be given some license to carry the ball forward and play line-breaking passes – which he has the skill set to do.

But at 22 years old, he does lack a bit of wisdom and has been guilty of running himself into trouble with overconfidence in possession. He will need to learn to pick the right moments to carry the ball, but that should come with experience – especially under the guidance of a top-quality coach.

Those who have followed Diomande closely during his time at Sporting told Daily Mail Sport that while the Ivorian exhibits a relaxed aura on the pitch, it has sometimes worked to his detriment – suffering blips in concentration.

That said, he does have know-how beyond his 22 years – making 87 appearances in the Portuguese top flight, 18 in the Champions League, 12 in the Europa League and earning 16 international caps including one at this summer's World Cup. He has silverware to show for it, too, winning the Portuguese top flight twice and the Portuguese Cup.

That was the precise reason he opted to join Sporting. The Portuguese outfit identified him while on loan at second-tier side Mafra from Denmark’s Midtjylland. Despite losing against Porto 3-0 in the cup, Diomande delivered a standout performance, drawing attention from the Sporting scouts. They passed a report to then-head coach Amorim, who immediately wanted to sign him.

He has significant Champions League experience with Sporting, as well as 16 caps for his country

‘We have to give credit to the people who discovered him,’ Amorim later said. ‘The scouting department showed me the player, and once I saw the details, it was immediately clear he was the one, whether he cost €500,000, €2m or €8m.

'He had all the characteristics - the way he played with the ball, his speed. And then there were other details, like going to the Dragao with Mafra and looking as if he was out in the playground. We knew what was there.’

When the January 2023 window opened, Sporting did exactly that, signing him in a £14m deal which will also see them pocket 10 per cent of the profit on this move, around £2.1m. Diomande credits Amorim with his career development and later revealed that the moment he was aware of Amorim’s interest, he wanted to make the move because of his faith in young players.

In Portugal, it was widely accepted that Diomande would eventually depart for one of Europe’s top five leagues. There was a slight surprise, however, that he did not wait for an even bigger move, as they believe he is destined for Europe’s elite. For Forest, that is a wonderful coup – especially if he follows his expected trajectory, which could see his value double in 2-3 years. There is also belief that once the mistakes are ironed out, he has the characteristics to be a leader.

Diomande suits Glasner, will have resale value if a bigger club does come calling and already demonstrated signs of becoming a supreme centre back - it is no wonder Forest want to make him the first marquee signing of the Glasner era. And, for the record, Gyokeres and Arsenal come to the City Ground on October 17. Get the fireworks ready.

Sports.title: Aston Villa in talks to sign another Chelsea outcast after Alejandro Garnacho - as Maxence Lacroix undergoes Blues medical ahead of £55m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

'Aladji adds depth and a range of qualities to our midfield options, with a huge potential for growth.

'His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and something we believe we can help him build on.

'He operates in a deeper role but has the ability to contribute all over the pitch, which he demonstrated in both Ligue Un and the Champions League last season.'

Meanwhile, Newcastle say they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

No Blues interest in Bruno

Chelsea are not expected to pursue a move for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

There had been suggestions that the West London club were interested in the Brazilian international, but Chelsea sources categorically refute this.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea have not, at any point, enquired about Guimaraes and sources maintain they have no plans to.

BOBBY MANZI

Boro target World Cup star

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA midfielder Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps.

Boro are paying £900,000 for the 25-year-old who has 18 caps and played in all of the USA's World Cup games.

The deal includes a further £600,000 in add-ons.

Berhalter was born in London where his father Gregg, a former USA coach, was a player at Crystal Palace.

Boro remain in talks for left-back Max Arfsten from Columbus Crew also.

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA star Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps

Sports.title: The crack coaching team Andoni Iraola has brought in to bring Liverpool back to the top: A 'fiery' fitness specialist to fight injuries, the solution to set-piece woes and Napoli's title-winning goalkeeping guru
Sports.content:
The crack coaching team Andoni Iraola has brought in to bring Liverpool back to the top: A 'fiery' fitness specialist to fight injuries, the solution to set-piece woes and Napoli's title-winning goalkeeping guru

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Liverpool fans are already growing used to the sight of Andoni Iraola as their new head coach but when he takes charge of his first match on Saturday in a friendly against Sunderland in Nashville, he will be flanked by several unfamiliar faces.

From a fitness coach that has been with him since way back, two former defenders with nearly 800 Football League appearances between them and a former Napoli goalkeeping guru, this is the team behind the Basque, who has been charged with taking Liverpool back to the top.

The first place to start is with right-hand man and Liverpool fan Tommy Elphick, who follows Iraola from Bournemouth alongside Shaun Cooper and Pablo de la Torre.

Scrolling back through the archives revealed an article from the Brighton Argus in 2011 when a young Elphick, then playing for the Seagulls in the Championship, said his ultimate dream was a trip to Anfield. Fifteen years on, he is finally there. Elphick takes his lessons in leadership from another former Bournemouth boss, Eddie Howe, who he played under as captain of the Cherries.

The 38-year-old is rated so highly that Championship clubs Bristol City and Burnley both reportedly made moves this summer to take him on as head coach. Elphick was a boisterous voice back in the day in a playing career that also saw him play for Aston Villa and Huddersfield – and sometimes was unclear what certain managers were asking of him. But the clarity of Howe’s messaging inspired Elphick to go into coaching when he was forced to retire at just 33 following his 10th operation.

Elphick was working as Under 21s manager at Bournemouth when his big break came in 2022-23. Gary O’Neil was promoted to head coach and Elphick was invited to form part of his backroom staff. ‘We went in, took the handbrake off and went for it,’ he said in 2023.

Andoni Iraola with Shaun Cooper (centre) and Tommy Elphick (right) in the Bournemouth dugout

Iraola has brought three of his Bournemouth colleagues with him to Anfield, where he is expected to bring Liverpool back to the top

When O’Neil was sacked despite keeping the Cherries up, Elphick knew that most of the squad felt disillusioned and that the decision was harsh. This was when the now 38-year-old earned his corn and sources say he was crucial in getting everybody back on board.

The new man, Iraola, had wanted to bring over his Rayo Vallecano No 2 Inigo Perez but it was not allowed due to a work permit issue. Perez has since taken the top job at Rayo and led them to the Europa Conference League final last season, earning him a move to Villarreal this summer.

Iraola likes to manage from a distance so Elphick and Cooper had a responsibility to take training sessions and to get to know players on a deeper level to help psychologically. When Bournemouth won none of their first nine games to start Iraola’s tenure, the coaches remained calm.

On a matchday, Iraola likes to sit in between Elphick and Cooper so he can get a constant dialogue. When the head coach’s voice runs out, he nudges one of the pair to bring some energy on the touchline.

Cooper is a set-piece specialist. It is understood the former Bournemouth, Sutton United and Portsmouth defender, born on the Isle of Wight, will focus on offensive, creative set plays while Elphick will take charge of defensive routines.

Set-pieces are a problem area for Liverpool, who conceded 23 goals from them last season, behind only Leeds, Crystal Palace and... Bournemouth. In late December, set-piece guru Aaron Briggs paid for it with his job, while set-piece analyst Lewis Mahoney stepped up and has earned plaudits for his work.

‘Shaun is coming up with loads of different set-pieces, he has new ones for us to try each game,’ said Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie. Last term, they scored 20 goals from set-pieces, ranking sixth, but at the other end had a problem, conceding the most in the division.

‘I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth,’ said Iraola when asked on this topic this week in Chicago. ‘They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different.

Elphick was forced to retire at just 33 due to injuries, after a playing career best known for his time playing under Eddie Howe at Bournemouth

Cooper (black trainers, centre right) will be tasked with being more hands-on than Iraola with the players

‘Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield, they can be in a closer position to the players, they can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn't know I was a player!

‘So they are very good to me, they are very good coaches, we kind of understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set-pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.’

Another important member of the new backroom team is De la Torre, a fitness coach who has been with Iraola since their time at AEK Larnaca in Cyprus.

‘Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching,’ explained Iraola. ‘So for me, he is much more than a physical coach, really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.’

He has been described as a ‘fiery character’ by local reports and De la Torre will have a big role this season as Iraola, for the first time, must get used to the constant demands of European football and competing on four fronts. Injuries were also a big problem last term.

De la Torre told Diario AS in Spain last month: ‘Seeing that daily evolution, football‑wise and human‑wise, is one of the proudest achievements of my career.

‘The key is building a game model and team identity where players truly believe in the coach’s idea. Beyond results, I’m proud to have been part of a group that never stopped believing, competing, and improving.

‘Andoni is incredibly intelligent, leads by example, and has a rare emotional stability in such a visceral sport. From day one, you sense he’s different — his ability to read the game and its needs is almost unique.’

Liverpool conceded 23 goals from set-pieces last season, including Amine Adli's last-minute winner for Bournemouth in January

Fitness coach Pablo de la Torre (left) has been with Iraola since their time at AEK Larnaca in Cyprus

Iraola will also have Luiz Fernando Iubel by his side. The Brazil-German dual citizen works across loans, Under 21s and Under 18s training groups and acts as a bit of a link man between all groups, which makes him important in pre-season especially for a joined-up pathway. Iubel was formerly assistant manager at Brazilian top-flight side Atletico Mineiro and joined midway through last season. He has supported Liverpool since being awestruck by their feats in the 2005 Champions League final.

His role is similar to that of Vitor Matos, one of Jurgen Klopp’s trusted backroom allies, who described it as ‘taking care of players that are between the first and second team’ and finding a pathway for them. Matos is now at Swansea.

Completing the backroom setup at Liverpool is new goalkeeper coach Alejandro Rosalen, who won two Serie A titles at Napoli. He replaces Xavi Valero, who lasted just one year in his second stint in the post.

Tom Webber joins as the first-team tactical analyst having replaced Roddy van der Ham. Webber went to the University of Birmingham and wrote a paper on the relative age effect in football – how people born after a certain cut-off, such as a school year or sports season starting, get physical and developmental advantages.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury fight LIVE: UK start time, how to watch and fight results
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury offered world title shot instead of Anthony Joshua fight

It looked like we were going to get Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury next, but WBC supremo Mauricio Sulaiman could throw a spanner in the works after revealing he would love to hand Fury a title shot before the end of the year.

He told Betway: "He's my friend. He's my dear friend. He was our champion for several years, a very proud WBC man, family man.

"We share values, we share special moments, and we speak often. So I'm very happy to hear that he's looking great. That video he sent ahead of England vs Mexico, he looked happy. He's just a unique individual. Kayabel vs Fury, that's a very doable fight, of course.

"Tyson Fury has been one of the greatest ambassadors, one of the proudest champions. I have a great respect for him and his family and his team.We had a great run for many years as our champion. Way, way back in 2011 or 2012, he was promoted by Mick Hennessy, and he had some sort of outburst, and my father had an exchange with him, and he apologised. Our relationship with Tyson Fury has lasted so long."

He added: "Maybe he doesn't even remember that. Then he wins, he beats Wladimir Klitschko, and falls into the deepest, darkest place that any human being can imagine. Then he comes out of it and becomes WBC champion.

"He's a hero for me, and I wish him well. I wish him the best always, and if he ever fights for the WBC title again, I will be there for sure. If he ever wins the WBC title again, I will be the proudest man to put the belt on Tyson Fury. He's a sensational representative of the WBC, and I love the man."

Surely we want to see Fury vs AJ more?!

Sports.title: Chelmsford racecourse saved after takeover with racing close to returning
Sports.content:
Chelmsford racecourse saved after takeover with racing close to returning

The Essex venue was shut in March when the BHA refused to issue a new licence after previous licence-holder went into administration

View 2 Images Chelmsford: set to reopen under ARC management (Image: PA)

Chelmsford racecourse has been saved after Britain’s largest racecourse group agreed a takeover of the troubled track.

‌



The Essex all-weather venue was shut in March when the BHA refused to issue a new licence after the previous licenceholder went into administration.

‌



It is the second time the track has been closed after first opening as Great Leighs racecourse in 2008 only to cease racing a year later. It reopened as Chelmsford City racecourse in 2015 but ran into financial difficulties earlier this year which the operators hoped could be addressed through a restructure which would avoid any interruption to its racing programme.

‌



BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid READ MORE :

However Great Leighs Estates Limited went into administration and BHA rejected an application from new company Golden Mile Racing Limited to operate the track.

On Friday Arena Racing Company, which operates 16 racecourses and five greyhound tracks, announced an agreement had been struck between Arena Racing Company and freeholders Moulsham Hall Estates Ltd and the racecourse.

‌



View 2 Images Chelmsford: shut since March (Image: PA)

As result racing is close to resuming at the course with all parties set to enter a period of exclusivity in order to enter into a long term, legally binding, agreement.

ARC chief executive Martin Cruddace said: "Racing at Chelmsford City Racecourse is hugely important to the fixture list and we are therefore delighted to work with the freeholders to reach agreement that will allow racing to return to the venue.

Article continues below

"We are in discussion with BHA with regards to the relevant licences required to resume racing as soon as possible."

Sports.title: Kristian Prenga’s pal has predicted a shock vs Anthony Joshua - he’s not wrong
Sports.content:
Kristian Prenga’s pal has predicted a shock vs Anthony Joshua - he’s not wrong

Anthony Joshua faces Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night, knowing a win will set up the long-awaited British heavyweight showdown with Tyson Fury

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua faces Kristian Prenga this weekend

According to Kristian Prenga’s sparring partner, we could be in for a shock on Saturday night.

‌



I agree. The shock in Saudi Arabia will register as water in the eyes of Prenga when that big right hand from Anthony Joshua hits the target.

‌



Though he stands 6ft 5ins, Prenga is neither a conventional dangerman nor an elite performer. He’s upright. He doesn’t bob and weave. He is essentially a big, novice pro, nice jab, reasonably quick hands, but as soon as he gets hit it’s good night Irene.

‌



This bloke has not fought anybody remotely in the class of Joshua. And as far as causing an upset, he is certainly no Daniel Dubois or Andy Ruiz.

And even in those contests, Joshua was in control before walking on to punches. He had Ruiz down and certainly shook Dubois before getting caught. Neither were sustained beatings.

Yes he lost twice to Usyk, but again, that is of little relevance on Saturday, a fact Prenga will realise soon enough. When you get properly hit by an elite fighter your pupils double in size.

‌



You feel it and your opponent can see it. It is then about how you respond. I fought a guy called Jean Marc Renard in my third pro fight. He hit me with a long left then a right over the top.

I went down but the shock of it made me 100 times more determined. It’s like a switch that twitches. Depending on your constitution, you get up, your head clears, and you go to work.

View 2 Images Prenga could be in for a shock on Saturday night

‌



There is no evidence in Prenga’s record to suggest he can cope with what’s coming. And that’s the point really.

Prenga’s team are looking at the fact that Joshua has fought just once in the past 22 months, and then only against blue-collar fighter Jake Paul. This is also Joshua’s first engagement since the loss of two close friends in the tragic car accident last December.

Above all Joshua is a prize fighter. Of course it will be emotional but he knows how to separate the personal and the professional on fight night. This, ultimately, is about setting up the next date in his diary appointment, and we all know what that is.

‌



Let’s not kid ourselves, Joshua will take a look at this guy then knock him out, just like he did Paul.

And then roll on Tyson Fury in November, something we can all get excited about.

Sports.title: The race King Charles wants to win ‘more than anything’, according to Royal trainer’s Mum
Sports.content:
The race King Charles wants to win ‘more than anything’, according to Royal trainer’s Mum

Ciaron Maher’s mother spilled the beans on her trip to Royal Ascot in June when she had lunch at Windsor Castle and got to ride in the royal procession

View 2 Images The Melbourne Cup: one of the biggest races in the world (Image: Getty Images)

King Charles has revealed there is one race he wants to win ‘more than anything else’, according to a royal trainer’s Mum.

‌



The King and Queen inherited the royal racehorse string from the late Queen Elizabeth II who had a lifelong passion for horse racing. Despite questions over the future of the Royal Family’s involvement in horse racing following Queen Elizabeth’s death, the King and Queen have maintained the tradition with a smaller yet effective string.

‌



In 2023 they celebrated their first Royal Ascot winner together when Desert Hero won the King George V Stakes and when the horse contested the St Leger they went to Doncaster to cheer him on.

‌



BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid READ MORE :

They also have a handful of horses based in Australia, including three with top trainer Ciaron Maher.

During Royal Ascot, Maher was invited to Windsor Castle for lunch with the King and Queen and were then given the honour of arriving at the racecourse in a horse drawn carriage as part of the royal procession. His plus-one was his mother Eileen who sat next to King Charles at lunch.

‌



Mrs Maher has now spilled the beans on their conversation, giving an interview in Australia to the SENTrack & RSN’s Giddy Up programme.

View 2 Images Eileen Maher with son Ciaron (right) (Image: Getty Images)

“During the lunch he happened to tell me that the Queen asked him to continue the legacy that she had started of having horses trained in other countries,” she said.

Article continues below

“She told him that it was a way of connecting with those communities and a way of keeping in touch. That is why Charles continued by giving Ciaron three horses to train.”

Maher has two potential stayers, Gilded Water and Aeolian, in his stable which are owned by the King and Queen.

Revealing more of her chat with the King, Eileen went on: “He told me that the race that he wants to win more than anything else is the Melbourne Cup, and if Ciaron could get one of those horses into the Melbourne Cup, he and Queen Camilla would definitely come out for the race.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury drops retirement bombshell ahead of Mariusz Wach fight amid Anthony Joshua plans
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury drops retirement bombshell ahead of Mariusz Wach fight amid Anthony Joshua plans

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are due to fight this year finally - with both returning to the ring this week as part of their preparations for facing each other

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has made clear that his boxing career is now almost over (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury claims this year will be the last of his career. The Gypsy King faces Mariusz Wach in Thailand today and is due to fight Anthony Joshua before the end of 2026.

‌



Fury, 37, retired for the sixth time last January before again reversing that decision barely a year later. The former unified heavyweight world champion returned to the ring after 16 months away in April with a unanimous decision victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

‌



Fury fights Wach a day before Joshua takes on Kristian Prenga, with the British duo expected to face each other later this year. It is Joshua's first bout since last he was involved in a devastating car crash last year, which saw his two close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami pass away.

‌



Anthony Joshua makes offer to Tyson Fury ahead of mega-fight READ MORE :

New venue emerges for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury mega-fight READ MORE :

Speaking before his second fight of 2026, Fury told The Sun: "This is my final year. That's why I want to be active. I don't want to go on until I'm 65 years old." He then confirmed: "This is the last year, yeah. Final year, 26."

Fury hinted at a busy autumn and winter, saying: "I just want to keep busy, keep active. It's not about money, it's not about belts, it's about nothing now.

"It's about enjoying my life and enjoying my career and doing what I love to do. That's boxing training, so maybe I'll do quite a lot this year."

‌



View 2 Images Tyson Fury fights Mariusz Wach today

Fury has not fought more than twice in a calendar year since 2018. On that occasion, he was also coming out of retirement, after two-and-a-half years away.

There were two warm-up fights against Francesco Pianeta and Sefer Seferi in the summer before taking on Deontay Wilder. If he is to fight four times in 2026 and rematch Joshua, that would be the first time he has done so since 2011.

‌



Fury was fighting for British and Commonwealth titles at the time, beating Derek Chisora for those two belts. However, one of those bouts was over ten rounds, rather than 12.

He has had only one 10-round fight since then, against Francis Ngannou three years ago. Any bout with Joshua would also presumably not be over anything less than 12 rounds.

Joshua's promoter has previously said that the contract specifies the United Kingdom. Al-Sheikh acknowledged earlier this month that Wembley Stadium would be his preferred host this month.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan fans' bid for 'fitting tribute' to England legend in Scunthorpe where career began
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan fans' bid for 'fitting tribute' to England legend in Scunthorpe where career began

Keegan, known to fans as King Kev, enjoyed a glittering career, which saw him win 63 England caps, including 31 as captain and win an array of trophies, including two Ballon d’Ors

View 4 Images Keegan sadly died on Monday aged 75 just months after revealing he had been diagnosed with cancer (Image: Colin Lane/Liverpool Echo)

Football fans are fundraising for a statue to honour Kevin Keegan in the place he began his career after he died following a battle with cancer.

‌



The proposed likeness would be placed in Scunthorpe, North Lincs, where the two-time Ballon-D'Or winner began his career, making more than 100 appearances, before moving to Liverpool for £33,000 in 1971. David Beverley, vice chairman of supporters group The Iron Trust, who are leading the fundraiser, said the statue would be a "fitting tribute" to King Kev, who went on to become a legend of the game.

‌



He said: "You've got to remember his career started here. He'd been rejected by Coventry City and Doncaster Rovers before Ron Ashman, who again was a legend at the club, saw Kevin, got him signed and then sold him to Liverpool in 1971."

‌



View 4 Images Kevin Keegan back in Scunthorpe for a fundraising game in May 1982 (Image: Scunthorpe Evening Telegraph)

Kevin Keegan shared three things people will remember him for in heartbreaking final interview READ MORE :

Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved READ MORE :

Keegan, who died on Monday aged 75, also went on to play for Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle during an illustrious playing career, which also included 63 England caps, including 31 as captain. He won three league Division One titles, the European Cup, two Uefa Cups and the FA Cup with Liverpool.

He later joined Hamburg, where he won the Bundesliga and back-to-back Ballons d’Ors in 1978 and 1979 – becoming one of only four English players to win the award, and the only one to do it twice. He also went on to manage England, as well as Newcastle, Fulham, and Manchester City, but despite his incredible success, Keegan still remained a supporter of Scunthorpe and repeatedly returned there to help raise funds.

‌



His last visit came in December last year when he attended the club's National League match against Tamworth, even giving a speech in the dressing room before the match, visiting the boardroom and meeting fans around the ground, including in the club's Iron Bar.

View 4 Images Keegan reunited with fellow Scunthorpe legends Ron Ashman (left) and Jack Brownsword during one of his returns to the club some years ago (Image: Scunthorpe Telegraph)

Current players and staff held a minute's applause and laid flowers in tribute to the former Iron player there earlier this week. And a book of condolence has now been set up at the Attis Arena, where an old quote from Keegan saying: "People think that the club that made me was Liverpool, but the club that really made me was Scunthorpe United", is on permanent display.

‌



Steven Plumtree, 55, was among those who visited to sign the book of condolence, which is surrounded by pictures of Keegan during his time playing at the club, as well as a candle. Mr Plumtree recalled watching Keegan play for the club and described his death as a "big loss to Scunthorpe". He said: "I thought I'd just come down and say goodbye to him in the best way."

Jamie Benson, 28, who also signed the book, said Keegan had "Scunthorpe in his heart". He said: "He still came to visit people. He was just down to earth and genuine and I think that's why so many people fell in love with him."

The fundraiser says: "The Iron Trust is fundraising for a Kevin Keegan memorial statue at the birthplace of his glittering career, in Scunthorpe, North Lincolnshire. We are raising funds to commemorate the great, late, Kevin Keegan, following the sad news of his passing on the 20th July, aged 75, with a people's memorial and statue to be located in Scunthorpe, the home of the Iron, the club at which Kevin began his football career."

Article continues below

View 4 Images Kevin Keegan signing autographs prior to the opening of Glanford Park, then Scunthorpe United's new ground, in 1988 (Image: scunthorpe telegraph)

It adds: "The Iron Trust invites fans of Scunthorpe United, Liverpool, Hamburg SV, Southampton and Newcastle, as well as football fans around the world to donate towards a lasting memorial at the birthplace of King Kev's extraordinary football career."

Sports.title: Argentina forced to make change as FIFA ruling emerges after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina forced to make change as FIFA ruling emerges after World Cup final

Argentina's disgraced team will be forced to make a change following their World Cup final loss

View 3 Images Argentina must make an alteration following the World Cup (Image: Getty)

Argentina are set to be given another brutal reminder of their devastating World Cup final defeat. The thuggish and negative tactics employed by Lionel Scaloni's side proved in vain as Spain clinched a deserved victory thanks to Ferran Torres's extra-time strike.

‌



Argentina had been aiming to lift the trophy for the fourth time in their history after Lionel Messi inspired the team to glory at Qatar 2022. Since becoming world champions, their strip had featured a gold crest displaying an outline of the trophy alongside the words "FIFA World Champions 2022".

‌



However, that prized addition to their iconic colour scheme must now be removed, as they are no longer world champions. Spain will now don the coveted emblem at the next World Cup, which they will co-host with Portugal and Morocco, with special one-off opening matches taking place in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the 100th anniversary of the World Cup.

‌



Argentina can at least continue to display a badge commemorating their Copa America victory in 2024, a title they will defend in 2028.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Argentina failed to relinquish the World Cup trophy or the gold badge with any grace. Leandro Paredes, along with team-mate Nahuel Molina and Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, were involved in the brawl seconds after the final whistle at the MetLife Stadium.

‌



Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow READ MORE :

Argentina FA intervene as World Cup final conspiracy theories emerge after Spain win READ MORE :

Contrary to the belief at the time, Paredes was not shown a red card following the incident. But FIFA has announced that its disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate possible breaches of the FIFA disciplinary code.

The South Americans attracted further condemnation for their combative style, with Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez sent off for two yellow cards.

View 3 Images Argentina must give up the gold badge in the centre of their shirt (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A FIFA statement read: "Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents."

Retrospective punishments, such as fines and/or suspensions, are possible for the country's federation or individuals. However, Spain midfielder Gavi, who was grabbed by Paredes during the post-match melee, insists he doesn't not want the Boca Juniors star to be hit with a ban.

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes drags Gavi to the floor (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

‌



Gavi told El Partidazo de COPE: "I don't think [Paredes] should be suspended. I understand it's not a good image for children, but I think there's also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

"The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that's it. In the end, I think it's all football, and it has to be that way."

Sports.title: Three Man Utd coaches have all given their opinion on JJ Gabriel
Sports.content:
Three Man Utd coaches have all given their opinion on JJ Gabriel

JJ Gabriel is in the Manchester United squad to face Rosenborg in Trondheim on Friday and could make his senior debut

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has been made to wait for his senior Manchester United debut (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel could make his first team debut for the club in Friday's pre-season friendly against Rosenborg. The 15-year-old has joined the likes of Harry Maguire and Bryan Mbeumo in a squad packed with senior talent in Norway.

‌



Gabriel is unsurprisingly the youngest member of the squad but fans expect him to more than hold his own. This is, in part, due to the glowing praise he has received from multiple coaches at Old Trafford.

‌



Manager Michael Carrick has given the teenager a chance to train with the senior squad in the past. Were it not for Premier League rules, Gabriel might have emulated the likes of Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri in playing top-flight football before his 16th birthday.

‌



Former caretaker boss Darren Fletcher has similarly had big things to say about a player who bagged 23 goals in the Under-18 Premier League last season. Carrick and Fletcher aren't the only ones, either.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer READ MORE :

Man Utd may have to scrap strict Arsenal transfer rule after latest Marcus Rashford blow READ MORE :

Head of academy Stephen Torpey joined United in 2025 and was clearly excited. "We have some special talents right now in our groups, and JJ is one of those, for sure," Torpey said.

‌



In March, Carrick admitted Gabriel wasn't allowed to play Premier League football but that didn't stop his glowing account of the youngster. "JJ is a big talent, it's pretty obvious to know that and he's had a really good season for the Under-18s," said the manager, who has since been installed on a permanent basis.

"We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development as we do with all the different younger players and picking the right moment to step up," Carrick continued. "What he's done when he's trained, he's done well as you'd expect and it's good to have the younger players come up with us."

View 2 Images Gabriel has had chances to train with United's senior squad (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Fletcher, who has worked with Gabriel at Under-18s level, has perhaps unsurprisingly been blown away by the talent. He suggested the player would have been ready for first-team football last season had such a thing been permitted, also indicating in May that a pre-season opportunity was unlikely to faze him.

"JJ's an amazing talent and has an enthusiasm for football that he brings to the pitch every day: to learn, to want to play and be on the ball," the Scot told The Athletic. "He's been a pleasure to work with. He's a fantastic kid."

He also suggested United planned to be careful when it comes to the teenager's first-team exposure, adding: "Once you get thrown in there, you're judged very, very quickly, rightly or wrongly. It's important that we do right by his development.

‌



"JJ's more than capable to go in, as are a lot of our young players. They all get experiences with the first team. It goes under the radar how many of our young players get tastes of the first team."

Gabriel is not the only teenager in the squad set to face Rosenborg, though he is the youngest of the bunch. Several others have already had a taste of senior football, including 18-year-old striker Chido Obi and Fletcher's 19-year-old twin sons Jack and Tyler.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
