World.title: President to swear in new judge to Poland’s disputed constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has agreed to swear in a new judge to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), ending weeks of doubt as to whether the opposition-aligned president would accept the judge appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority. Although Sławomir Patyra will now be accepted onto the court, four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year continue to be excluded after Nawrocki refused to receive their oaths and the TK’s chief justice, also aligned with the opposition, blocked them from taking office. W najbliższy wtorek 28 lipca Prezydent Karol Nawrocki działając na postawie art. 4 ust. 1 ustawy o statusie sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, przyjmie ślubowanie od prof. Sławomira Patyry i tego samego dnia wręczy powołania czterem nowym sędziom Sądu Najwyższego. W przyszłym… — Zbigniew Bogucki🇵🇱 (@BoguckiZbigniew) July 22, 2026 Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK – for example when a judge’s nine-year term expires – the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again this week, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. Patyra himself has also made clear on which side of the dispute he stands. In an interview with news website Onet in May, he accused Nawrocki and Święczkowski of “blatantly unlawful actions” in deciding which TK judges can and cannot take office and suggested that the police should intervene. Sędzia TK prof. Patyra po raz kolejny zaapelował do Prezydenta o wyznaczenie mu terminu na złożenie przysięgi. Ignorowanie sędziego TK przez Prezydenta jest kolejnym przykładem psucia państwa. To pokazuje, jak bardzo siły anty-demokratyczne boją się odbudowy niezależnego TK.… — Dariusz Mazur (@_Dariusz_Mazur) July 21, 2026 Finally, on Wednesday this week, Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, announced that Nawrocki had invited Patyra to the presidential palace on Tuesday next week to take his oath. Speaking to Polsat News, Bogucki said that, in the case of Patyra, initially “there were some doubts, but the president dispelled them”, without specifying what they were. In the end, they concluded that “we had a fundamentally clean situation here” and Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”, unlike the six new judges chosen by the Sejm in March to fill longstanding vacancies. “It was not President Nawrocki or the current opposition who destroyed and are destroying the tribunal; it is the government that is doing it,” he added. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. World.title: Germany deploys soldiers to Poland to help reinforce eastern borders
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany has deployed soldiers to Poland to help reinforce defences on NATO’s eastern flank in response to the threat of Russia. While Poland already hosts various allied forces, the presence of German troops is particularly symbolic given the two countries’ difficult history. “United, we will prevail,” wrote the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces (SGWP), announcing the deployment. “This is what allied cooperation looks like in practice, which translates into greater military readiness and strengthens NATO’s defensive potential.” Polscy i niemieccy żołnierze razem wzmacniają granicę z Rosją. Takie rzeczy możliwe tylko za Tuska ☺️ pic.twitter.com/oNBME2gBsv — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 22, 2026 Last December, the Polish and German defence ministries revealed that a “mid-double-digit number” of German troops would be deployed from mid-2026 until the end of 2027 to support implementation of Poland’s East Shield operation, which seeks to bolster defences along the borders with Belarus and Russia. They said that the German personnel would mainly engage in engineering work, such as digging trenches, laying barbed wire and constructing anti-tank barriers. Today, Poland’s SGWP confirmed that “several dozen” German troops, including “highly specialised engineering forces” along with their equipment, had since June been temporarily deployed to “support the Polish armed forces in expanding defence infrastructure on NATO’s northeastern flank”. It emphasised that the East Shield project is “purely defensive in nature” and comes in “response to threats stemming from, among others, Russian aggression against Ukraine”. While the armed forces did not reveal the location of the deployment, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk indicated in a social media post that it was on the Russian border. Poland has a 210-km frontier with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. German public broadcaster Deutsche Welle reports that the activities of the German sappers are focused in particular on improving defences around the so-called Suwałki Gap, a strategically important stretch of land around the Polish-Lithuanian border between Belarus and Kaliningrad. “Together, we are ensuring Europe’s security,” said Lieutenant General Alexander Sollfrank, the Bundeswehr’s operational commander, announcing the deployment today. “Through our engagement in Poland, we are strengthening NATO’s defence capabilities and underscoring the alliance’s unwavering commitment to ensuring peace through unity and credible deterrence.” Poland and Germany have signed a bilateral security agreement that will see the two neighbours and NATO allies increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity https://t.co/6BPX2WxvxH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 17, 2026 SGWP, which shared footage of Polish and German forces installing anti-tank barriers, said the work aims to “hinder and delay an aggressor’s actions in the event of a threat”, thereby “increasing the time for a response from the Polish armed forces and the entire [NATO] alliance”. It also seeks to “create conditions for the efficient reception, deployment and use of NATO forces on Polish territory”. SGWP welcomed “the involvement of the German contingent as a practical expression of allied solidarity and the result of consistently developing military cooperation between Poland and Germany”. It also noted that the cooperation would help the two sides improve their ability to operate jointly, including “developing the competencies necessary for conducting a joint defence operation”. However, it emphasised that the current deployment is focused on training and engineering, with no combat component, and that the German troops are unarmed. SGWP also emphasised that the East Shield operation remains entirely a Polish national programme. The leaders of eight countries on the EU's eastern flank have met in the first summit of its kind to discuss closer security cooperation. Finland and Poland announced that they would jointly lead an initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, to bolster defences https://t.co/fxRHpkM6w9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 The deployment of German troops to Poland comes shortly after the two countries signed a defence cooperation agreement in which they pledged to increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity. The agreement is a sign that the two countries now stand “shoulder to shoulder, as equals”, declared German defence minister Boris Pistorius. Poland is also currently seeking a new permanent US military base on its territory, after President Donald Trump recently pledged to boost American troop numbers. Last week, Tusk also announced that Poland will host military exercises involving France and the UK this autumn. Poland will host military exercises later this year with France and the UK to prepare for providing future security guarantees to Ukraine, says PM @donaldtusk. He also declared Poland's willingness to permanently host more troops from its European allies https://t.co/couian4FrP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 14, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches first of 11 planned “community forests” around major cities
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s climate and environment ministry has inaugurated the first of 11 planned “community forests” around large cities, with the aim of giving residents a place for recreation and contact with nature while also helping to fulfil the government’s pledge to reduce logging. Plans for the forests were announced in 2024, and the first has now been established around Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city. Ten other major urban centres, including Warsaw, Kraków, Poznań and Łódź, are set to follow. Dotrzymujemy słowa. Powołaliśmy pierwsze lasy społeczne w Polsce, to lasy ochronne wokół Wrocławia. Kolejne miasta przed nami. @MKiS_GOV_PL pic.twitter.com/RxhsMZShj9 — Paulina Hennig-Kloska (@hennigkloska) July 21, 2026 “This is a historic moment and the beginning of a new approach to forest protection – with residents in mind first and foremost,” said climate and environment minister Paulina Hennig-Kloska at an inauguration ceremony outside Wrocław on Sunday. “Community forests are places where residents can relax, play sports and simply spend time close to nature,” she added. “At the same time, they are crucial to our security and quality of life: they retain water, regulate the climate, purify the air and protect the soil.” An area covering 13,000 hectares (32,124 acres) has been designated as a community forest around Wrocław. Forest management there will now be aimed at “maximising the forest’s social functions”, says the ministry, while timber harvesting is also restricted. The area will be divided into three zones, including “natural forests”, where nature will be left to take its course, and “near-natural forests” with minimal intervention. However, the largest zone, amounting to over 8,000 hectares, will be “social forests”, which the state forestry agency says “will be managed in a way that ensures the comfort of those who use the forest and its benefits related to wellbeing, physical exercise and recreation”. Hennig-Kloska noted that, in the latter area, educational trails as well as hiking and cycling paths would be established. However, given that such facilities already exist in many forests, it remains unclear how the new community forests will differ. The ministry is now conducting consultations and analysis on establishing community forests around ten other designated urban centres: Bielsko-Biała, Tricity (Gdańsk-Gdynia-Sopot), Katowice, Kielce, Kraków, Łódź, Poznań, Szczecin, Toruń-Bydgoszcz and Warsaw. On Sunday, Hennig-Kloska said that the “next in line” to have their community forests established are Kielce and Bielsko-Biała, reported the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Shortly after coming to power in December 2023, the current government announced that it would halt planned logging in some forests. The former Law and Justice (PiS) administration had faced criticism for overseeing an increase in logging, especially in Białowieża Forest. The current government also launched plans to create Poland’s first new national parks in over two decades. However, PiS-aligned President Karol Nawrocki last year vetoed that move, arguing that it would “block the economic development of the region” and threaten Poland’s security. President Nawrocki has vetoed government plans to create Poland’s first national park in 24 years Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argues that the park would “block economic development of the region” and threaten Poland’s security https://t.co/v3aMzT9ok8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 8, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland joins EU satellite project developing European alternative to Starlink
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has joined a European Union project developing a secure satellite internet service that would provide an alternative to networks such as Elon Musk’s Starlink. Warsaw has committed €656 million (2.8 billion zloty) to the IRIS² programme, with the money coming from Poland’s EU post-pandemic recovery funds. In return for joining the project, Poland will gain access to the secure satellite communications network for government institutions, the armed forces and emergency services, while the growing Polish space industry will be eligible to compete for contracts linked to the development of the constellation Today Poland🇵🇱joins the EU🇪🇺space programme #IRIS² w/additional €656 mln. 🇵🇱 is on a remarkable space journey to build a strong space economy & secure connectivity for the defence of Poland, the Eastern Flank & 🇪🇺. IRIS² brings greater unity & strength for the entire Europe. pic.twitter.com/TwS59vpXtm — Andrius Kubilius (@KubiliusA) July 21, 2026 “This is a big day for Poland, the eastern flank and the entire European Union,” declared the EU’s defence and space commissioner, Andrius Kubilius, at a signing ceremony in Warsaw on Tuesday. “By investing in space, Poland is investing in its security, its economy and its future.” Speaking alongside him, Poland’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said that IRIS² would help “ensure our security and strategic independence” while “demonstrating that Poland aims to be a leader in the European space industry and remain at the centre of EU security efforts”. “No single country is able to build such a [satellite] constellation so efficiently, which is why we are joining this major project – to be part of it and one of its managers,” he added. The IRIS² programme aims to deploy a constellation of nearly 300 satellites in low and medium Earth orbit, providing encrypted, interference-resistant communications for governments, defence agencies, emergency services and selected commercial users across the EU. First announced in 2022, the project is part of the EU’s efforts to reduce dependence on non-European satellite operators amid growing concerns over cybersecurity, hybrid threats and the resilience of critical infrastructure following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. “It is super important for Europe to have a sovereign capacity, and Starlink will never do that,” said Eva Berneke, CEO of Eutelsat, one of the companies involved in the project, quoted by Politico Europe. The project is expected to cost €10.6 billion, including €6.5 billion in public funding and around €4 billion from private investors. World.title: Meet the Four Prague Pizzerias Recognized in 50 Top Pizza Europa 2026
World.content:
Prague’s growing pizza scene gained international attention after four local restaurants were recognized in the 50 Top Pizza Europa 2026 guide.

The biggest success went to Pizza Nuova, which secured 30th place among the best pizzerias in Europe outside Italy. While the restaurant slipped a few places compared with last year’s ranking, it remains the only Czech establishment to appear in the guide’s main European list.

Located near Prague’s Kotva department store, Pizza Nuova has built its reputation on authentic Neapolitan pizza made with premium Italian ingredients. The restaurant also holds certification from the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana, an organization that promotes traditional Neapolitan pizza-making standards.

Prague’s recognition extended beyond a single restaurant. Three additional venues received the guide’s Excellent Pizzerias distinction, awarded to restaurants that consistently demonstrate outstanding quality.

This year’s recipients are Da Pietro, Sasy The Original, and Diskotéka in Prague’s Dejvice district.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Pizzeria Da Pietro Praha (@dapietropraha)

Diskotéka is one of this year’s notable newcomers. Shortly after opening, the restaurant attracted attention for its distinctive interior, centered around a large silver pizza oven designed to resemble a disco ball.

Alongside its food, the venue hosts DJ nights and combines a traditional pizzeria with a relaxed social gathering space.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diskotéka Pizza (@diskoteka.pizza)

The annual 50 Top Pizza rankings are compiled by anonymous inspectors who visit restaurants without prior notice. Their assessments go well beyond the pizza itself, taking into account ingredient quality, dough preparation, baking technique, service, beverage selection, atmosphere, and the overall dining experience.

World.title: Czech Women Earn About CZK 109,000 Less Per Year Than Men
World.content:
Czech women earn significantly less than men on average, with the annual difference estimated at CZK 109,000.

New figures based on Eurostat data show the country’s gender pay gap remains above the EU average.

Across the EU, employed women earn an estimated CZK 93,800 less annually than men on average. The European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC), which converted the hourly wage gap into annual earnings, estimates that the combined difference across the bloc amounts to more than CZK 8.65 trillion every year.

Czech Republic exceeds the EU average

According to Eurostat, women across the European Union earned 11.1% less per hour than men in 2024. In practical terms, women received CZK 88.90 for every CZK 100 earned by men. The figures cover companies with at least ten employees.

Applying that methodology, the ETUC estimates that women in the Czech Republic earn roughly CZK 108,700 less per year than men, placing the country above the EU average.

Only a handful of member states recorded larger estimated annual gaps. Finland ranked highest at around CZK 183,500, followed by Austria (CZK 165,600), Germany (CZK 146,200) and Sweden (CZK 123,600).

At the opposite end of the scale, Luxembourg was the only EU country where women earned slightly more than men on average. There, women’s hourly earnings exceeded men’s by 0.8%, equivalent to roughly CZK 11,500 annually in their favor under the ETUC model. Estonia recorded the largest percentage gap in the bloc, at 18.8%.

Different methods produce different figures

National Czech statistics paint a somewhat different picture because they rely on a different methodology.

Data from the Czech Statistical Office shows that in 2025 the median gross monthly wage reached CZK 41,068 for women and CZK 47,648 for men. That represents a monthly difference of CZK 6,580, or just under CZK 79,000 over a full year.

The discrepancy does not mean either calculation is incorrect. Eurostat measures average gross hourly earnings, while the Czech Statistical Office compares median monthly wages. Because the indicators measure different aspects of income, the results cannot be directly compared.

Eurostat uses an unadjusted gender pay gap, which reflects a range of labor market factors, including differences in occupations, industries, management roles, work experience, career interruptions, age and the balance between public and private sector employment.

World.title: Spicy, Not Spicy: How This Chef Is Bringing Authentic Chinese Street Food to Prague
World.content:
At Manifesto Market, the aroma of Sichuan peppercorns and chili oil stands out among the usual mix of street food and drinks.

It comes from Lá Bù Lá Street, the more casual sibling of the restaurant Lá Bù Lá, both founded by Wen, a Chongqing native who wants to introduce Prague diners to the real flavors of her hometown.

Wen arrived in Prague in 2019 after being accepted into a Master’s program at the Prague University of Economics and Business. But studying was only part of the reason she moved. At 22, she wanted a new beginning and the chance to discover a different version of herself.

“There was something about Prague that attracted me immediately,” she says. “The architecture, the pace of life, the atmosphere of the city —

it all felt very charming. I wanted to see what kind of person I could become here.”

That decision eventually led her into the restaurant business, with four concepts launched over the years — two that closed and two that continue today.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lá Bù Lá Street (@labula_street)

Beyond the Stereotypes

For Wen, opening a Chinese restaurant in Prague was never only about selling food. It was also about showing people that Chinese cuisine is far more diverse than many stereotypes suggest.

“China is a huge country, and every region has its own culture and food traditions,” she says. Through her restaurants, she hopes guests become more curious about where dishes come from, how ingredients are used, and how different regions eat.

She also wants Chinese food to be seen as something connected to special occasions, not only a quick meal.

“Chinese food can create beautiful memories too,” she says. One example is Chongqing chili, which is often associated only with heat. Wen says there is much more to it.

“Many people think Chongqing chili is only about being spicy. But it is also about aroma,” she explains. The same applies to Sichuan peppercorns, where the famous numbing sensation is only part of the experience.

Learning the Hard Way

Wen’s path has not been simple. Her first two projects, Chi Xiao Mian and Mi I’m, did not succeed as she had hoped, but she sees them as important lessons.

“They taught me how to work with people, how to manage a team, and how important communication is,” she says.

The experience also taught her to stay focused on her original vision. Running a restaurant requires listening to others, but also knowing when to trust your own ideas.

“Building something meaningful always requires finding a balance between dreams and reality,” she says.

A Restaurant, and Then a Street

Today, Wen runs two concepts: Lá Bù Lá and Lá Bù Lá Street. The name, meaning “spicy, not spicy,” reflects the idea that Chongqing cuisine is about much more than just heat.

The original restaurant offers a deeper introduction to traditional Chongqing dishes, while Lá Bù Lá Street at Manifesto Market has a more relaxed atmosphere.

“It is more spontaneous and more social,” Wen says. The concept is inspired by street food culture in Chongqing, where people gather, share dishes, and spend time together.

At Manifesto, surrounded by music, travelers, and international crowds, the idea has naturally evolved. Some dishes work better for sharing, while others simply encourage people to stay longer.

“For us, food tastes better when shared,” Wen says. “Passed around a table. Offered to a friend. Or quietly stolen from someone else’s plate.”

Growing Step by Step

Like many restaurant owners, Wen faces daily challenges, from managing a team to introducing unfamiliar flavors to new customers. Building a group of people who share her values has been one of the most difficult parts.

When asked about opening more locations in Prague, she says the ambition is there — but there is no rush.

“Of course, I would love for more people to discover the food of my hometown,” she says. “But I am not in a hurry.”

For now, Wen is focused on improving the restaurants she already has and building a stronger team.

“When my team and I are truly ready, we can always begin the next journey,” she says. “For now, we are happy to keep growing step by step.”

World.title: Prague and Stockholm Launch Cross-Border Public Art Project
World.content:
Visitors in Prague and Stockholm will soon be able to communicate across borders through a pair of interactive public art installations designed to exchange anonymous messages between the two cities.

The linked installations, created by the Czech initiative Praho! project and its Swedish partner Stockholm! project, will open in Stockholm on August 20 and in Prague on August 31.

The installations are designed as private spaces intended for one visitor at a time.

After entering, participants answer a series of questions before listening to an authentic audio recording left by someone in the other city. They are then invited to record their own message, creating an ongoing exchange between residents and visitors in Prague and Stockholm.

According to the project team, the concept explores what happens when anonymous thoughts become personal through the human voice.

“The installation creates a space where you first listen to someone else—and only then can you speak,” the organizers said. “We want to explore how connecting two different cities through shared experiences can foster understanding.”

The initiative is part of Art & Design Without Borders, an international collaboration supported by the Erasmus+ programme. The project brings together organizations from the Czech Republic and Sweden to promote participatory art, community engagement and new approaches to public space.

Although they work closely together, Praho! project and Stockholm! project operate as independent non-profit organizations. Their partnership reflects a shared history rather than a branch structure.

Praho! project was founded in 2021 and focuses on participatory art in public and digital spaces. Through text-based interventions and an online platform, it has collected more than 30,000 anonymous responses addressing personal experiences and broader social issues. Those contributions have since been transformed into publications, exhibitions and artistic installations.

The concept, however, began even earlier. Founder Annamarie Čermáková first developed the idea in 2019 while studying at Stockholm University of the Arts. Returning to Sweden inspired the creation of Stockholm! project in 2025.

The project extends beyond the installations themselves. Organizers will also host workshops, educational programmes, international internships and prepare a methodology guide documenting best practices in participatory public art across different European settings.

World.title: BAY55: 114 Luxury Apartments Planned for Prague’s Riverfront in Smíchov
World.content:
One of the last undeveloped riverfront plots in central Prague is set to become home to a new luxury residential project.

Developer Daramis has unveiled plans for BAY55, a development featuring 114 high-end apartments on Hořejší nábřeží in Smíchov, just steps from the railway bridge and within walking distance of the city center.

According to Daramis, BAY55 is designed to compete with premium residential developments in leading European and North American cities. The company says the project will emphasize architecture, technology, privacy and resident services alongside its prime location.

The residence will include a wellness and fitness center covering roughly 600 square meters, a private residents’ lounge and hospitality facilities.

A restaurant or café is also planned on the ground floor, serving both residents and visitors. The developer says the level of amenities is intended to match those found in luxury hotels.

Designers have also focused on balancing density with comfort. Every apartment is planned to include either a spacious balcony or terrace, complemented by integrated shading systems intended to provide greater privacy despite the urban setting.

Before construction of the residential complex can begin, significant work will be carried out along the riverfront.

The existing Smíchov embankment will be extended, creating additional public space and improving pedestrian access along the Vltava. The infrastructure upgrades are expected to become part of the wider transformation of one of Prague’s fastest-growing neighborhoods.

Daramis acquired the land from BPD Development in 2024. Although the developer has not disclosed the value of the investment, it says BAY55 represents the largest and most expensive project in the company’s history.

Costs are driven not only by the location and construction standards, but also by flood protection measures, advanced building technologies and architectural features planned for the shared spaces.

The project is currently progressing through the permitting process. If approvals proceed as expected, construction of the new embankment will begin first, followed by the residential development itself.

Completion is currently scheduled for around 2030.

World.title: From Müller to Krispy Kreme, Global Chains Are Coming to Czechia
World.content:
International drugstores, fashion retailers, discount chains and restaurant concepts are preparing to open their first locations in Czechia, adding new competition for established players.

Here are some of the biggest brands expected to enter the Czech market.

Müller

German retailer Müller is preparing to launch in the Czech Republic. The company has already established a Czech branch and website, although it has not yet announced the opening date of its first store.

Unlike traditional drugstores, Müller combines cosmetics and personal care products with toys, stationery, household goods, pet supplies and organic food.

The chain operates nearly 1,000 stores across nine European countries and will compete with established Czech market leaders such as dm, Rossmann and Teta.

Krispy Kreme

American doughnut chain Krispy Kreme is reportedly searching for a location in central Prague and could open its first Czech store soon.

Founded in North Carolina in 1937, the company became famous worldwide for its Original Glazed doughnuts and stores where customers can watch the production process.

Ochnik

Polish fashion brand Ochnik plans an ambitious expansion in the Czech Republic, with 15 to 20 stores expected by the end of 2026.

The company specializes in leather jackets, footwear, luggage and accessories. It previously considered acquiring Czech brand Kara but decided to build its own network instead.

OVS

Italian fashion retailer OVS is also preparing its Czech debut.

The company focuses on affordable clothing for the whole family and is particularly strong in children’s fashion. It is positioned between discount retailers and mainstream brands such as H&M, C&A and Reserved.

Normal

Danish discount chain Normal is preparing to enter the Czech market after establishing a local company.

The retailer sells cosmetics, household products, snacks and everyday goods at permanently low prices. Its stores are designed to encourage impulse shopping, with customers walking through a changing selection of products.

MR. D.I.Y.

Malaysian discount retailer MR. D.I.Y. has some of the biggest expansion plans among new arrivals.

The company plans to open around 20 stores in Prague and eventually grow to more than 100 locations across the Czech Republic. Its first Czech store is expected to open at Forum Nová Karolina in Ostrava.

MR. D.I.Y. sells household equipment, DIY products, electronics and stationery.

Burgermeister

Berlin burger chain Burgermeister will enter the Czech Republic as part of its European expansion.

The brand started in 2006 inside a converted toilet building near Berlin’s Schlesisches Tor station before growing into a chain with more than 30 restaurants.

It focuses on its own production, including burgers made with Irish beef and ingredients prepared in Berlin.

Dave’s Hot Chicken

American fast-food chain Dave’s Hot Chicken is preparing to compete with KFC and Popeyes in the Czech market.

The brand specializes in Nashville-style spicy fried chicken, offering chicken tenders and sandwiches with different levels of heat.

Founded in Los Angeles in 2017, the chain has expanded to more than 400 locations worldwide.

Arthur Gelato

Slovak premium ice cream brand Arthur Gelato has already opened its first Prague location on Francouzská Street.

The company focuses on handmade ice cream, fresh ingredients and unusual flavors. It plans further expansion through franchising.

Sticks’n’Sushi

Danish restaurant group Sticks’n’Sushi will open its first Prague location this autumn.

The concept combines Japanese sushi with grilled skewers and will operate a three-story restaurant on Jungmann Square with around 160 seats.

World.title: Five Things to Know Before Flying From Prague Airport This Summer
World.content:
Passengers departing from Prague Airport this summer are being advised to plan ahead as the airport prepares for its busiest travel season in years.

To help travelers avoid unnecessary delays, the airport has released a list of practical recommendations covering transport, security screening, travel documents and baggage rules.

Leave Extra Time to Reach the Airport

The biggest challenge this summer is expected to be road access to the terminals. Construction at the Aviatická–Lipská intersection may cause traffic congestion on routes leading to the airport.

Airport officials recommend using public transport whenever possible, as buses are not affected by the roadworks. Travelers arriving by car should allow extra time to reach the terminals, particularly during peak holiday periods.

Self-Service Check-In Can Save Time

Passengers can speed up the departure process by using the airport’s self-service facilities. Prague Airport now offers 31 check-in kiosks and 32 self-service baggage drop counters, available for flights operated by 18 participating airlines.

Before heading to the airport, travelers should also verify the entry requirements for their destination. Those flying to the United Kingdom, for example, now need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before departure.

Bring Physical Travel Documents

Although many travelers rely on digital wallets and electronic documents, Prague Airport reminds passengers that electronic IDs and passports cannot be used during passport control.

Travelers should carry a valid physical passport or national identity card, depending on the requirements of their destination.

Security Rules Depend on the Terminal

Passengers departing from Terminal 2 will notice a faster security process thanks to newly installed CT scanners.

The new technology allows travelers to leave electronics and liquids inside their cabin baggage during screening. In addition to the standard one-liter transparent bag containing containers of up to 100 milliliters each, passengers may also carry one extra liquid container with a capacity of up to two liters.

These updated rules currently apply only in Terminal 2. Security procedures in Terminal 1 remain unchanged.

Pack Power Banks Correctly

The airport is also reminding travelers about one of the most common packing mistakes.

Power banks, laptops and tablets must always be transported in carry-on baggage, not checked luggage. In addition, lithium batteries must not exceed 100 Wh unless specifically approved by the airline. Ignoring these rules can lead to delays during security checks or, in some cases, passengers being refused boarding.

World.title: Czechia Debates Social Media Ban for Children as France Moves Ahead
World.content:
France is moving toward stricter rules on children’s use of social networks, while a similar debate is gaining attention in the Czech Republic.

Lawmakers, educators and experts are increasingly discussing whether children should face age restrictions on social media and tighter limits on smartphone use in schools.

The issue has grown across Europe amid concerns about excessive screen time, cyberbullying, online safety and children’s exposure to unsuitable content.

France has become one of the first European countries to push forward with legislation that would prevent children under the age of 15 from creating accounts on social media platforms. The French Senate has approved the proposal, which still requires approval from the lower house of parliament before it can become law.

If adopted, the measure would take effect on September 1 and require online platforms to introduce age verification systems. Companies would also have to remove accounts belonging to underage users within four months.

The French proposal also includes restrictions on mobile phone use in secondary schools, reflecting a wider European discussion about the role of smartphones in children’s lives.

Czech Republic considers stricter rules for smartphones in schools

The Czech Republic has so far focused mainly on regulating mobile phone use during school hours rather than banning social media accounts for children.

This week, the Czech government backed a proposal that would introduce a nationwide restriction on the use of mobile phones and other electronic communication devices in schools. The regulation is expected to come into force in September 2027.

Concerns over gaming, online content and cyberbullying

Supporters of stricter rules argue that unrestricted access to smartphones can expose children to risks ranging from harmful online content to addictive behaviour.

Experts have raised concerns about easy access to pornography, excessive gaming and the development of unhealthy digital habits among young users.

Many Czech schools have already introduced their own rules. Some require students to hand in their phones when they arrive, while others collect devices at the beginning of lessons.

Several European countries, including Spain and Denmark, are preparing similar measures aimed at protecting children online.

World.title: New details in the Hatvanpuszta zebra scandal: illegal keeping, escaped animals, and carcasses dumped in a pig pit
World.content:
László Gajdos, the minister responsible for animal welfare, has ordered a full investigation into the zebras kept at a farm between Bicske and Hatvanpuszta in western Hungary, he said on Facebook on Friday.

In the post, Gajdos said the relevant official documents reflected “total chaos” in the case, adding that “one thing is certain: there has been no responsible ownership there”. He said some of the zebras had arrived at the farm with inadequate documentation and that permits were applied for only later. The owners did not apply at all for a special licence for five of the animals, he added as per the Hungarian news agency.

Of the 17 zebras, only 10 had been registered, he said. He added that one of them, called Tihamér, had been kept illegally and that his existence only came to light after his death. He also said there had been no proper fence, and that three of the animals escaped and froze to death. Moreover, he said, the carcasses were disposed of illegally and thrown into a pit for pigs that had died of swine fever.

Screenshot from Gulyáságyú Média/YouTube

“This is not animal protection, but grave irresponsibility … we will not leave it at that,” Gajdos said. He also added that there are currently 17 adult zebras and three foals at the farm.

World.title: Hungarian lawyers’ circle head: former PM Orbán may soon become a suspect – can he be arrested?
World.content:
The head of the Lawyers’ Circle, Lóránt Horváth, said on the programme Konkrétan with Egon Rónai that he is convinced the case of the Ukrainian gold convoy lies behind the resignation of chief prosecutor Gábor Bálint Nagy, and that the affair could eventually reach Orbán himself.

Gold convoy case: are Hungarian authorities failing to investigate at full strength?

According to Horváth, while the chief prosecutor cited moral reasons for his departure, financial and economic considerations may also have played a role. He said that after his resignation there follows a 30-day notice period, after which Gábor Bálint Nagy could continue working as a prosecutor on a net salary of 2.5 million forints, whereas a removal procedure would also put his prosecutorial status and related benefits at risk. The lawyer therefore said that removal proceedings should be initiated even during the notice period, since the chief prosecutor continues to exercise full powers during that time, the Hungarian News Agency wrote.

The former premier is currently attending the Tusványos festival in Transylvania, Central Romania. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

Speaking about the gold convoy case, Lóránt Horváth claimed that the investigation had omitted steps that would have been justified in a case of comparable gravity. In his view, organised offending appears to be taking shape, and investigators should either have worked their way up to the leadership level or gathered evidence from the bottom up. Instead, he said, the chain of responsibility was “cut in the middle” and János Hajdu, the former head of the Counter-Terrorism Centre, was placed at the centre of the case. Although he was charged, Horváth said that, given the gravity of the case, detention, house searches and the seizure of IT equipment could also have been warranted.

The scandal may reach former PM Orbán

The lawyer also claimed that in cases of this magnitude, investigating prosecutors brief the chief prosecutor on a daily basis, meaning he can know about every important investigative step and issue instructions as well. In his opinion, the new chief prosecutor, while reviewing the cases of the past year, may find numerous circumstances suggesting interference in the proceedings.

Former PM Orbán in Brussels on a press conference. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

Lóránt Horváth said he believed the threads of the case lead to Orbán, and that if this is proved, it could have criminal significance. He said a political will had been tried to present as a criminal offence, but this had not fully materialised. In his view, no crime had in fact been committed, but rather an operation organised on a political order, for campaign purposes, of which the prime minister was most likely also aware. He added, however, that questioning or charging Orbán would require an incriminating statement or other evidence.

Will former anti-terrorism chief Hajdu face jail instead of ex-PM Orbán? Alleged aim of secret meeting revealed

They turned to the press deliberately

The programme also touched on János Hajdu’s testimony. Horváth said that, to his knowledge, Örs Farkas, who previously supervised the civilian national security services, had not yet been questioned, but that he could soon be heard as a suspect.

Orbán and Hajdu on the morning of the gold convoy operation. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

The lawyer also said that the Ukrainian bank had regained the seized assets, and that he himself was present at their handover. According to him, a few items remained in the money-laundering investigation, and their return had also been requested. He said that the expulsion measures imposed on those concerned had also been withdrawn, so they can once again move freely within the territory of the European Union.

Lóránt Horváth said ensuring publicity for the case had been a deliberate legal strategy, at the request of their client, because otherwise the gold convoy affair would, in his view, have been lost among the other proceedings.

World.title: German tourist drowns in popular Hungarian lake
World.content:
Hungarian police have launched an investigation after a German tourist drowned in Lake Hévíz, a popular tourist destination in Hungary. Authorities say he attempted to swim in the thermal water in a prohibited area.

According to hvg.hu, the German national entered the lake’s outflow at a restricted point. The Zala County Police Headquarters said they were notified on 22 July that a body had been found in Lake Hévíz. It later emerged that the 41-year-old man had decided the previous evening to swim in the thermal water. However, he drowned for reasons that have yet to be determined. The Keszthely Police Department is investigating the circumstances of the incident.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Police have also warned that swimming is permitted only in designated areas. In other parts of the lake, swimmers may encounter hazards that are not immediately visible. “Complying with the rules is not an unnecessary obligation but serves to protect life. Unfortunately, tragedies occur every year that could have been prevented with a single responsible decision.”

According to Pénzcentrum, more than 40 people have already drowned in Hungary this year.

World.title: Epstein scandal reaches Hungary again after unexpected death of agent who hunted out Hungarian girls
World.content:
The Epstein scandal has reached Hungary once more with the sudden death of a model scout who allegedly searched for girls in the country, as the ripples of the affair continue to shake even the old British royal establishment. Daniel Siad, 69, was under investigation in France by prosecutors specialising in human trafficking, on suspicion of rape and other offences, but had not yet been questioned. His body was found at home, and investigators have ordered an autopsy.

Very close to each other

Siad’s name appears more than a thousand times in the US Department of Justice Epstein files released this year. The documents suggest that the model scout worked closely with Jeffrey Epstein for years, regularly finding women from the fashion industry for him while the billionaire covered his travel costs on several occasions through bank transfers.

According to the files, Siad travelled through villages in Eastern Europe, but also went to Cuba and Sweden in search of models. In a 2014 email, he compared his work to fishing, saying patience was needed because “sometimes you catch fish quickly, sometimes nothing” — in rather poor English, as The Guardian noted. On the basis of the Epstein files, he remained in contact with the billionaire until 2016.

Photo: his photo uploaded to the registry of sexual offenders. Source: Wikimedia Commons.

Hungary in the files

The released documents do not only shed light on Siad’s activities; they also contain several Hungary-related references. In one 2009 email, Siad asked the billionaire for money so he could spend the following months in Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary, where, in his own words, he wanted to look for girls in “small villages”. He ended the message by saying he would have “a big surprise” when Epstein arrived in Paris, though it was never made clear what he meant.

The correspondence also shows that in 2015 Epstein asked Siad in an email what had happened to “the Hungarian girl”. Several other emails refer to Hungarian girls, as well as to a Hungarian woman who sent Epstein photographs and videos, then wrote that she had cut ties with “Daniel’s friend” because he had treated her badly.

Budapest keeps appearing

Budapest also crops up repeatedly in the millions of Epstein documents released in January. The papers show Epstein corresponding with the Norwegian film producer Haakon Gundersen, who has Hungarian links, about the transfer and sale of a flat at 70 Király Street in Budapest, Telex reported at the time. The emails also suggest that Epstein repeatedly indicated he was heading to Budapest, or was already in the city.

Short messages in the files include:

“I’ll send someone to Budapest.”

“I’ll be in Budapest.”

“I’m in Budapest. On my way to you.”

“I’m in Budapest. Which flat?”

The documents do not, however, show exactly when those trips took place. After Telex published its report, Gundersen’s production company issued a statement denying that he had any business or other relationship with the American billionaire. The statement said Epstein had never been to any property or business connected to Gundersen.

Hungarian names and models

The files also mention the literary agent John Brockman recommending network scientist Albert-László Barabási to Epstein in 2012. Epstein wanted to meet him and contacted him by email in 2014, but the planned meeting never happened. After the documents were made public, Barabási said he had not known the correspondence would be released, that he had never met him, and that there was no further contact beyond the brief email exchange in 2014.

Another document says Epstein sent a package to economist János Kornai in 2005, though the files do not reveal what it contained.

Owner of Budapest property linked to Epstein files says he was threatened

The documents also name two Hungarian top models. In a 2013 email exchange, businessman Tancredi Marchiolo asked Epstein whether he knew Barbara Palvin, and the billionaire replied that he did not. Enikő Mihalik’s name appears in a 2017 message, when he asked an acquaintance whether he had seen attractive women at a New York gym; Mihalik was mentioned in the reply, along with a note about the models present.

Cause of death under review

Daniel Siad had previously denied all allegations against him. He said he had only introduced women to Epstein through legitimate model castings and did not know the billionaire was committing crimes. According to Siad, he had not supplied either minors or adults who became victims of sexual offences. He also told French television that Epstein had abused his trust and that he was not in a position to recognise the danger.

After his death, French authorities opened an inquiry to determine the cause, and an autopsy has been ordered.

Epstein himself has been dead since 2019, after hanging himself in his cell following a second arrest on serious charges.

Hungarian names emerge in Epstein files: models, recruiters and Eastern Europe

World.title: Record numbers admitted to Hungarian universities, including thousands of international students — what comes next?
World.content:
More than 101,000 students are set to begin higher education at Hungarian universities this September, including a significant number from abroad. We have gathered the key points newly admitted students need to watch, the most popular universities and courses, and what the new government is promising those embarking on their studies.

Admission thresholds for 2026 have been published nationwide for 140,427 applicants, while 101,572 students have received text messages confirming where they will begin their studies in just over six weeks’ time, the Minister for Education and Children announced on social media.

Judit Lannert noted that 77,853 students secured state-funded places. The most popular field of study is business and economics, with 21,274 admissions, while the single most sought-after course is business administration and management, attracting 5,929 students, according to the Hungarian news agency MTI.

The moments of tense waiting. Photo: Facebook/Lannert Judit

Government pledges international opportunities

The admission rate this year stands at 72 per cent, meaning nearly three-quarters of applicants have been accepted, the Ministry for Education and Children said.

Reforming higher education is a long-term investment in Hungary’s future, the ministry stressed, aiming to ensure universities offer competitive knowledge, modern research environments and international opportunities.

And the first cries of happiness. Photo: Facebook/Lannert Judit

Most popular universities and courses

The leading fields this year are business and economics (21,274 students), teacher training (16,199), engineering (13,314), humanities (9,855), IT (7,753), social sciences (7,447), and medical and health sciences (7,432).

The most popular courses include:

Business administration and management (5,929)

Master-level teacher training (3,845)

Law (3,811)

Nursing and patient care (3,185)

Commerce and marketing (3,036)

Special education (2,800)

Teacher training continues to grow, with 16,199 admissions this year. A record 4,656 students have enrolled in primary teaching (2,039) and undivided teacher training programmes (2,617).

Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) once again admits the largest number of students, with 13,723 entrants, while three technically focused institutions also feature in the top ten.

The highest entry score was required for Corvinus University’s English-language international business programme, followed by ELTE law (467 points), Pázmány Péter Catholic University law (467), Pázmány psychology (462), Corvinus international studies in English (459), and ELTE psychology (455).

Although the latest report does not specify the number of newly admitted foreign nationals, preliminary statistics from the Central Statistical Office show that 49,458 international students studied in Hungary in the 2025/2026 academic year, the vast majority — 46,813 — in full-time programmes.

At Corvinus, 990 students were admitted through international procedures, either self-funded or via bilateral scholarship schemes. ELTE reported that 1,059 new students will begin English-language courses this September, while the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (MATE) expects more than 700 foreign students across its English-language programmes.

Scramble for rentals as prices surge

University cities remain key hotspots in Hungary’s property market, characterised by strong rental demand and rising prices. Following the publication of admission thresholds, rents may increase by up to 5 per cent over the summer, according to Zsolt Molnár of MBH Mortgage Bank.

Gábor Soóki-Tóth of Otthon Centrum added that the market may ease by October, with prices falling by 2–4 per cent.

In Budapest, monthly rents near university hubs range between 205,000 and 304,000 forints, with District VII the cheapest and District IX the most expensive. Over the past five years, rents have risen by at least 50 per cent — and in some areas have doubled.

Among provincial cities, Debrecen stands out with average rents around 200,000 forints, while Szeged and Pécs hover near 150,000.

Who gets the house? Property inheritance in Hungary for international owners

Demand spikes sharply after results are announced, with enquiries rising by around 30 per cent, said András Pásztor of Fundamenta Ingatlan.

Molnár added that property prices per square metre in university cities have nearly doubled over the past five years.

Rent or buy?

For those planning to stay longer than five years, buying is generally more economical than renting, according to Pásztor. For shorter periods, renting remains the better option.

With market-rate loans, purchasing in Budapest typically only becomes more cost-effective after more than ten years. In major provincial cities, the timeframe is similar, though in Miskolc it may be as short as five years. With subsidised financing and partial letting, this period can shrink to three to five years.

Planning to stay for years in Hungary? Maybe you should consider buying instead of renting. Photo: depositphotos.com

Hungarian house prices remain among the fastest-growing in Europe: since 2015, they have quadrupled, compared with an EU average increase of just 65 per cent, said Flóra Horti of MBH’s analytical centre. Growth is expected to moderate, with nationwide price rises of 8–13 per cent forecast for 2026.

A longstanding shortage of student accommodation continues to push many towards the private rental market.

Property market weakens in Hungary, but above average market still holds on

World.title: Black Coffee in Budapest: Grammy-winning DJ returns after 12 years
World.content:
Black Coffee in Budapest is set to become one of the Hungarian capital’s most exclusive electronic music events of the summer. The Grammy-winning South African DJ will perform at Buda Castle on 14 August 2026, returning to the city after a 12-year absence for an intimate open-air show limited to just 2,000 guests.

Budapest has no shortage of spectacular venues, but few can compete with the drama of a summer night inside the historic Buda Castle complex. For one evening, the stately Lion Courtyard – known in Hungarian as Oroszlános Udvar – will exchange its usual royal atmosphere for hypnotic rhythms, sophisticated electronic sound and a carefully curated club experience.

According to Time Out Budapest, the performance will be Black Coffee’s first appearance in the Hungarian capital for 12 years. With admission capped at 2,000 people, the event promises a far more intimate setting than the major festivals, arenas and celebrated Ibiza venues where the artist regularly performs.

Black Coffee in Budapest after a 12-year absence

Black Coffee has played a defining role in taking South African electronic music to a global audience. His sets combine deep house, Afro house, restrained vocals and African musical influences, building an atmosphere that is elegant, gradual and immersive rather than relying on predictable festival-style drops.

That distinctive approach has made him one of the most recognisable figures in international electronic music. His career has included major festival appearances, high-profile residencies and performances at some of the world’s best-known venues.

His 2021 album Subconsciously won Best Dance/Electronic Album at the 2022 Grammy Awards. The victory also made him the first African artist to win the category with an original project, further strengthening his status as a leading figure in contemporary dance music.

In May 2026, he also presented his ambitious Live With Orchestra production at London’s O2 Arena, demonstrating how comfortably his music can move between underground club culture and large-scale artistic performance.

If you missed it – Skip the tourist crowds: 7 secret thermal baths in Hungary most foreign visitors never discover

A royal setting for an exclusive electronic music event

The location is likely to be just as memorable as the artist. Buda Castle stands on Castle Hill above the River Danube and forms part of Budapest’s UNESCO World Heritage area, alongside the historic riverbanks and Andrássy Avenue. For international visitors, it is one of the most important architectural and cultural landmarks in the Hungarian capital, UNESCO World Heritage Centre said.

The Lion Courtyard is situated within the Buda Castle complex at Szent György Square in Budapest’s 1st District. Surrounded by monumental historic façades, it offers a markedly different atmosphere from a conventional nightclub or festival field.

Against this backdrop, the Black Coffee in Budapest show is expected to combine heritage, panoramic surroundings and contemporary nightlife in a way few European events can match. The contrast between the centuries-old setting and Black Coffee’s polished, modern sound is precisely what gives the evening its premium character.

The event is being organised by Hungary’s City Takeover in cooperation with Croatian promoter BSH Events, which specialises in staging electronic music performances at unusual and monumental locations. Before travelling to Budapest, Black Coffee is also scheduled to perform at the Roman amphitheatre in Pula, Croatia. The Buda Castle show will be BSH Events’ first production in Hungary.

Tickets and essential information

The event will take place on Friday, 14 August 2026, at the Lion Courtyard of Buda Castle, located at 2 Szent György Square, 1014 Budapest. Gates are scheduled to open at 6 pm. The show is strictly for visitors aged 18 and over, and guests must present valid photographic identification upon entry.

Ticket prices were advertised as starting from EUR 70, approximately HUF 25,000, although availability and individual ticket categories may change as the date approaches.

With only 2,000 places available, Black Coffee’s return is shaping up to be more than another date in Budapest’s busy summer calendar. It will offer a rare chance to experience one of the world’s leading electronic artists in a setting that captures the capital at its most historic, atmospheric and unmistakably elegant.

World.title: Don’t Miss: F1 Events in Budapest
World.content:
Although the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix takes place at the Hungaroring, fans can also attend numerous related events in the capital. Most of these are free, but since it’s hard to keep track of them all, we’ve put together an overview of these events.

Written by Tamás Szikora

Formula 1 Cars in Budapest

Numerous so-called show cars and replicas are on display in the Hungarian capital, and there’s even a life-size LEGO model to see. What’s more, almost every one of these exhibitions is accompanied by exciting programs and attractions, each of which guarantees a unique atmosphere for visitors.

Audi R26 Show Car – Széllkapu-Millenáris Park

This year, Audi became the latest automaker to join the Formula 1 grid. Anyone who wants to see the German brand’s show car with their own eyes should visit Millenáris. In addition to the Audi Revolut F1® Team R26 show car, visitors can also view the new Audi RS 5 and the new Audi Q3. Both are manufactured at the Audi Hungaria plant in Győr. Even an engine manufactured at the Győr plant will be on display as a special exhibit, and an Audi Pop-up Store will open on site, offering the official Audi Revolut F1® Team collection and exclusive Audi merchandise.

In addition, the Hungarian Grand Prix will be broadcast live at the Zsiráf in Buda as part of the Audi F1 Fanzone. The Saturday evening program is particularly worth checking out, featuring a roundtable discussion with Gergely Makai, the FIA’s official photographer, and Gábor Wéber, an M4 Sport commentator, during which audience members will also have the opportunity to ask questions.

Address: 1024 Budapest, Margit körút 85–87

Open: July 24–26.

(Social link)

BWT Alpine F1 Team – Time Out Market

If you’d like to see the Alpine F1 Team’s race car, visit the Time Out Market. But fans will find more than just the car on display there. There’s a BWT water bar and water tasting station, a themed photo wall with prizes, various exclusive offers, and you can even request laser engraving on BWT Climate Bottles, as well as purchase other BWT and BWT Alpine F1 Team fan merchandise.

You can also watch live TV broadcasts of the weekend’s F1 races here, so no one has to miss out on the excitement, and fan meet-and-greets will be held throughout the entire week of the Hungarian Grand Prix. On Tuesday, Formula 2 driver Gabriele Mini was in attendance, and on Thursday, a meet-and-greet was organized with Alpine’s two F1 drivers, Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

Address: 1085 Budapest, Blaha Lujza Square 1.

Open to the public: July 22–26.

(Social link)

Life-Size LEGO F1 Ferrari – Alza Showroom

During the drivers’ parade at the 2025 Miami Grand Prix, LEGO’s massive creations were a huge hit; powered by electric motors, they reached speeds of up to 20 km/h. The model, which replicates a Ferrari F1 car, was built by a team of 26 people using nearly 400,000 pieces at LEGO’s factory in the Czech Republic. It is currently on display at Alza’s showroom in Hungary, where it will remain on display for quite some time. The exhibition runs through August 10, but there are plenty of other events to look forward to in the meantime.

Simulator races will be held, and during breaks, visitors are free to practice on the Logitech simulator and the Logitech G McLaren gaming seats. All of this takes place within the official F1 ’26 game, on the Hungaroring track. On July 25 and 26, as well as August 1 and 2, an administrator will be on site to record the results. It’s worth giving it a try, because the winner will have the opportunity to participate in the Logitech G Race Days gaming event. The finals will take place in Barcelona in the fall of 2026. But that’s not all: Alza’s showroom features a unique exhibition showcasing models built from LEGO® sets specifically for this event, and there’s also a photo corner for kids.

Address: 54–58 Róbert Károly sugárút, 1134 Budapest.

Open to the public: July 10–August 10.

(Social link)

Boxutca Experience Week – Westend

Similar events have been held in the past, but this year a replica of the Ferrari F1 car will once again be on display at Westend. Thanks to the Italian team’s partners, Peroni and Shell, visitors can view the car at the shopping center, where exciting activities await them throughout the week.

It’s definitely worth spending some time here this weekend, as visitors can participate in prize giveaways, a pit-stop competition, simulator and reflex games, and sample Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%. There’s also the Shell V-Power zone, where technology takes center stage. One of the week’s most important events took place on Wednesday, featuring Antonio Giovinazzi, Ferrari’s current WEC driver and reserve driver for the F1 team.

Address: 1062 Budapest, Váci út 1–3.

Open: July 20–26.

(Social link)

Let’s cheer together in front of giant screens

Nothing can replace the experience of an F1 race weekend spent at the track, but not everyone has the opportunity to follow the events at the Hungaroring in person. That’s why you’ll be able to watch the free practice sessions, qualifying, and, of course, Sunday’s race on giant screens at several venues in and around Budapest. We’ve already mentioned Zsiráf Buda and Time Out Market, where this will be possible, but there are plenty of other options to choose from as well.

The Akvárium Klub, for example, is hosting an event called “F1 Terrace.” At this event, you can comfortably follow the action on the track from the terrace, and admission is free. The free practice sessions and the race of the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix will be broadcast on the giant LED screen on the terrace of Zsiráf Pest, as well as on the screen at Holdudvar on Margaret Island.

So if you’d like to watch the action on the track in good company, a great atmosphere, and on a huge screen, you have several options to choose from. But even if you’re planning such an outing exclusively for Sunday (perhaps extending into the evening), we still have a few suggestions for you. In Törökbálint, on the shores of Lake Nádas, the live broadcast will be available starting at 1:30 p.m., so no one will miss out on the buildup to the Hungarian Grand Prix. Throughout the day, you can try out the simulators, and the evening will conclude with special events. At 7:20 p.m., the Boda Family will take the stage, followed by a fantastic outdoor movie screening at 8:00 p.m. As part of the event, you can watch the Oscar-winning film *F1: The Movie*

Venues:

Akvárium Klub (1051 Budapest, Erzsébet tér 12)

Zsiráf Pest (1062 Budapest, Teréz krt. 53)

Zsiráf Buda (1024 Budapest, Kis Rókus utca 2–4)

Holdudvar (1138 Budapest, Hajós Alfréd sétány 1.)

Formula 1 Picnic (2045 Törökbálint, Nádas Lake)

SUBSCRIBE to our daily newsletter to never miss a bombshell!

Other Attractions

Numerous other events worth seeing await visitors, most of which are available exclusively during the Hungarian F1 Grand Prix weekend. These include events celebrating the 40-year history of the track and the race, as the Hungaroring opened its gates in 1986, and F1 made its first visit to Hungary that same year.

40 Years of the Hungaroring” Photo Exhibition – Széllkapu Park

This exhibition, one of the many exciting events taking place at Millenáris, opened in June but will only be on view through Sunday. Each of the photos on display captures the most important and iconic moments of the racetrack and the race. The exhibition is also a great opportunity to take a trip down memory lane, and it’s sure to get motorsports fans’ hearts racing.

(Social link)

F1 Installation and Flag Decorations

Recent years have proven that this definitely has its place during this time of year. The life-size F1 logo is located on Heroes’ Square and offers a fantastic opportunity to take stunning photos and selfies. Don’t miss the flags displayed at various locations throughout the city—on several of Budapest’s bridges and streets—all celebrating the Hungarian Grand Prix. Among others, the Erzsébet Bridge and the Margit Bridge have been decorated in this way. All of this will be on display until July 26.

(Social link)

Evening Light Show on Margaret Island

At the Musical Fountain on Margaret Island, a unique evening light show will be held several times leading up to the day of the Hungarian Grand Prix, paying special tribute to the race, which looks back on a 40-year history. The show begins every evening at 9:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. through Sunday, promising a pleasant, relaxing evening.

Hungaroring-themed sightseeing boat tour in Budapest

This program extends slightly beyond the race weekend, as MAHART Cruises Budapest’s uniquely painted boat will be on display through August 5. The boat’s design was inspired by the Hungaroring, and to further enhance the guests’ experience, they can also sample Hungarian Grand Prix-inspired cocktails during the Danube cruise.

Social link:

LEGO x W Budapest Exhibition – W Budapest

The exhibition, which has opened in the courtyard of the W Budapest hotel, is open not only to hotel guests but also to the general public. A truly impressive LEGO installation has been set up here, allowing many people to view the exhibition organized as part of DESIGN EXCHANGE x LEGO®: F1® EDITION, which features iconic race cars and helmets made from LEGO bricks. The exhibition will remain open for a little while longer, so if you can’t make it this weekend, you can still check it out until July 31.

Address: 1061 Budapest, Andrássy út 25

Hugo Racing Tour – Westend

Keep an eye out for the Hugo truck in front of Westend. The company remains a partner of the Racing Bulls team, and this time, together with Optic World, they’ve prepared plenty of surprises. Here you can try out the simulator—the best players can win prizes—and visitors can take part in a virtual eyewear fitting to find the model that suits them best. On Saturday night, a DJ and drinks await, there will be a photo booth, and of course, the Pit Stop challenge is a must.

If you missed it – At the Top of Motorsport: Audi Formula 1 show car displayed at SZE

World.title: Toshihiro Suzuki meets Péter Magyar and Viktor Orbán in Budapest
World.content:
Suzuki Hungary has returned to the centre of economic attention after the Japanese carmaker’s global president held separate talks with Prime Minister Péter Magyar and former prime minister Viktor Orbán. The discussions focused on potential investment, the electric transition and the wider challenges facing the international automotive industry.

Toshihiro Suzuki’s meetings underline the long-term importance of the Japanese manufacturer to Hungary. Suzuki has operated in the country for 35 years, while its Esztergom factory remains the group’s only European production base and one of the most established foreign investments in Hungarian manufacturing.

Péter Magyar discusses further Suzuki Hungary investment

Péter Magyar announced on Thursday that he had met Toshihiro Suzuki, president of Suzuki Motor Corporation.

According to HVG, the prime minister described Suzuki as one of Hungary’s most reliable foreign investors since the company established its local subsidiary in 1991.

Magyar said the talks covered possible further developments and investments in Hungary. The two sides also discussed the challenges facing the global automotive sector and the transition towards electric mobility.

No specific investment, production expansion or new model was announced following the meeting. Nevertheless, the subjects discussed are particularly relevant to Hungary, where vehicle manufacturing and the international supply chains connected to it represent a major part of industrial output and exports.

Suzuki currently manufactures the Vitara and S-Cross models at its Esztergom plant, including hybrid versions. Future decisions concerning electrification, production technology and model allocation could therefore have a direct impact on the position of the Hungarian facility within the wider Suzuki group.

Orbán meets the Suzuki president separately

Toshihiro Suzuki also held a separate meeting with Viktor Orbán at the Fidesz headquarters on Thursday.

The former prime minister and the Suzuki delegation exchanged views on the state of the global economy and the future prospects of the automotive industry, HVG reported, citing Bertalan Havasi, Fidesz’s communications director.

Orbán also met Toshihiro Suzuki in May 2025, when he was still serving as prime minister. That meeting took place at the Carmelite Monastery in Budapest and similarly focused on the manufacturer’s presence in Hungary and developments affecting the automotive sector.

The two meetings held on Thursday indicate that Suzuki continues to be regarded as an important economic partner in Hungary. The company’s investment decisions matter not only to Esztergom and its surrounding region, but also to Hungary’s export performance and its broader industrial strategy.

More than three decades of production in Esztergom

Magyar Suzuki was established in 1991 by Suzuki Motor Corporation, the Hungarian government, Itochu and the World Bank. Serial production began in Esztergom in 1992 with the five-door Swift, helping to revive passenger-car manufacturing in Hungary after a hiatus of almost 50 years.

The plant subsequently produced models including the Wagon R+, Ignis, SX4, Splash and several generations of the Swift. Today, production is centred on the Vitara and S-Cross.

The four-millionth vehicle manufactured in Esztergom rolled off the production line in February 2024. It was a hybrid Vitara, reflecting the plant’s increasing focus on lower-emission powertrains. Suzuki has invested more than EUR 2 billion in its Hungarian operation since the company was established.

The Esztergom facility is also the Suzuki group’s only vehicle manufacturing plant in Europe. This gives Suzuki Hungary a role extending beyond the domestic market: vehicles made in Hungary are supplied to more than 100 countries.

If you missed it – Japanese culture in Hungary: manga, anime and gastronomy met in Budapest

Suzuki Hungary remains a major exporter and employer

The company’s latest full-year figures demonstrate its economic weight. Magyar Suzuki produced 108,072 vehicles in Esztergom in 2025 and recorded total net sales revenue of EUR 2.059 billion.

Export sales generated EUR 1.774 billion, accounting for approximately 86% of the company’s total revenue. More than 92,000 vehicles built in Esztergom were exported, while the company employed an average of 2,833 people during the year.

Suzuki also retained its position as the leading brand on Hungary’s new passenger-car market in 2025. A total of 14,285 Suzuki vehicles were registered, giving the company an 11.04% market share. It was the 22nd year in which the brand finished first since serial production began in Esztergom.

Against this background, Toshihiro Suzuki’s meetings in Budapest were more than routine corporate visits. As European manufacturers face pressure to electrify production, reduce emissions and compete with rapidly expanding Asian rivals, Suzuki’s plans will remain closely watched in Hungary.

No immediate agreement was announced, but the talks highlighted a relationship that has endured for three and a half decades. The next phase of that relationship is likely to depend on further investment, technological modernisation and the place assigned to Esztergom in Suzuki’s transition towards electric mobility.
