Remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan and Ilocos Norte – waves up to 3.5 meters high

Northeastern seaboard of Isabela; northern seaboard of Ilocos Sur; eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental – waves up to 3 meters high

Up to moderate to rough seas (small vessels should take precautionary measures or avoid sailing, if possible)

Seaboards of Zambales and Surigao del Sur; northern seaboard of Aurora; western seaboard of Pangasinan; remaining seaboard of Isabela – waves up to 2.5 meters high

Seaboards of Cuyo Islands, Kalayaan Islands, Cagayancillo Islands, and Davao Occidental; northern. seaboards of La Union, Camarines Norte, and Camarines Sur; northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands and Catanduanes; eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon, Northern Samar, Eastern Samar, Dinagat Islands, and Siargao-Bucas Grande Islands; western seaboards of Bataan, Occidental Mindoro including Lubang Islands, mainland Palawan including Calamian Islands, and Negros Occidental; southern seaboards of Antique, Iloilo, Guimaras, Negros Oriental, Davao Oriental, and Sarangani; remaining seaboards of Ilocos Sur and Aurora – waves up to 2 meters high

Kiyapo is the Philippines’ 11th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the fourth for July alone.

Once outside PAR, Kiyapo may undergo rapid intensification and strengthen into a typhoon ahead of its expected landfall in mainland China during the weekend. But as it crosses China, a weakening trend is likely to begin. – Rappler.com

World.title: What do Filipinos want to hear from Marcos’ fifth SONA?
World.content:
SONA 2025. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr delivers his 4th State of the Nation Address, in the House of Representatives, on July 28, 2025.

A Pulse Asia survey conducted from late June to early July asked Filipinos which issues they would most like President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to discuss in his fifth State of the Nation Address

MANILA, Philippines – The fight against corruption is the most liked topic that Filipinos want to hear from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. when he delivers his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27.

This is among the findings of a Pulse Asia Research survey held from June 28 to July 3, but released only on Friday, July 24.

“For the President’s 27 July 2026 SONA, the top issue the public would like to hear him discuss or mention is his administration’s fight against corruption (29.8%), particularly efforts to investigate and hold accountable those involved in the flood control projects scandal (18.9%). This is followed closely by the issue of affordable basic goods (18.7%),” Pulse Asia said in a statement on Friday.

The highlight of Marcos’ SONA last year was his crackdown on flood control corruption, which led to a government probe.

Former senator Bong Revilla and Senator Jinggoy Estrada, among others, have been detained in a Quezon City jail over plunder charges in connection with the flood control mess, and the Ombudsman has identified the President’s cousin, former House speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez, as the “central figure” in the multi-billion flood control corruption scandal.

Other SONA topics listed by at least 1% of Filipino adults include the following:

Anti-corruption initiatives in general (10.9%)

Jobs and livelihood opportunities (6.6%)

Poverty (6.2%)

Illegal drugs (5.5%)

Low wages (5.1%)

High fuel prices (4.9%)

Agricultural issues (4%)

Criminality (2.8%)

State of education (2%)

Fulfilling presidential promises (1.6%)

Impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte (1.2%)

Juvenile justice (1%)

Senate leadership issue (1%)

Welfare of senior citizens (1%)

Among the issues that less than 1% of Filipinos would most like to hear in Marcos’s fifth SONA are improving public health (0.9%), peace and order (0.8%), case/situation of former president Rodrigo Duterte (0.7%), housing program (0.6%), reduced taxes/removal of taxes on basic commodities (0.6%), peace among bickering politicians (0.5%).

The survey period was prior to the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, which began on July 6.

This nationwide survey is based on a sample of 2,400 representative adults. It has a ± 2% error margin at the 95% confidence level, while subnational estimates for the geographic areas covered in the survey have the following error margins at 95% confidence level: ± 4% for Metro Manila, the rest of Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. – Rappler.com

World.title: Trump imposes forced labor duties on 60 trading partners, including Philippines
World.content:
DONAD TRUMP. US President Donald Trump speaks during the signing ceremony for an executive order on mail ballots, in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, USA, on March 31, 2026.

'We can still negotiate,' says Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel Romualdez in a message to Rappler, when asked whether Trump's decision was final

WASHINGTON, USA – The Trump administration on Friday imposed new tariffs of 10% and 12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, including Europe, China, the Philippines, over allegations of lax enforcement of forced labor bans, just as a temporary 10% global tariff expired.

The move is the White House’s latest effort to restore President Donald Trump’s vision of a near-global tariff after the US Supreme Court in February struck down his “reciprocal” duties of 10% to 50% imposed under a national emergencies law to try to shrink the US trade deficit.

New tariffs had been expected, but trade partners around the world joined in strongly disputing the justification for them. Some, however, noted they would make little difference to current levies. There was little early reaction on financial markets more focused on the Middle East conflict.

In a statement on Friday, the Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque said it takes note of the unilateral move, and that it would “continue to engage with the US” regarding the Philippines’ policy on forced labor.

“We note that this is based on the alleged failure to impose and effectively enforce prohibition of imports made by forced labor,” she said on Friday, July 24.

“The Philippines will continue to engage with the US to emphasize that the country has a strong policy against forced labor consistent with various International Labor Organizations (ILO) Conventions. In fact, just yesterday we signed a Joint Administrative Order with Department of Finance and Department of Labor and Employment to provide institutional mechanism to address the issue of forced labor,” Roque said.

Sought for comment, Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel “Babe” Romualdez said the Trump administration’s move was subject to talks.

“We can still negotiate,” he said in a message to Rappler, when asked if there was still wiggle room on the issue.

The new tariffs, announced in a Federal Register notice, cover 99.4% of US imports, but include numerous product exemptions, such as oil and gas, fertilizer and certain food items.

“The United States has had a forced labor import ban for nearly a century, and rigorously enforces it. It’s well past time for our trading partners to do the same,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement.

“Today’s action will begin to correct what is both a human rights abuse and distortive trade practice to improve the welfare of workers everywhere.”

Imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, the new duties allow the administration to maintain a tariff floor on virtually all US imports despite the Supreme Court setback. The tariffs are also likely to face less legal risk as Section 301 has survived prior court challenges.

Trump’s temporary 10% global tariff expired at 12:01 a.m. EDT on Friday (0401 GMT) after 150 days. The new duties took effect at that exact same moment, with goods in transit exempted until 12:01 am EDT on July 28.

The US imposed a 10% duty on goods of Argentina, Bangladesh, Britain, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago.

The European Union, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland were assigned rates that, combined with pre-existing most-favored-nation tariff rates, totaled 10% or 12.5%.

The other 38 countries were assigned a 12.5% rate. These include the Philippines, as well as Vietnam, which issued a new decree this week that sets out more detailed rules banning imports of goods made with forced labor, and China — accused by the US of detaining Uyghur minorities in work camps, which Beijing denies.

Greer previously pledged that for countries with trade deals with Washington capping US tariff rates, the new forced labor duties would not push them above those caps — a point which the EU noted in its response.

“The EU notes positively the fact that this outcome is in line with the US tariff commitments agreed under the EU-US Joint Statement,” a European Commission spokesperson said, adding it provided “positive momentum” to continue the work on exploring further tariff exemptions and deepening cooperation.

While disputing the allegations underlying the forced labor investigation, the Swiss government also said the United States was adhering to past commitments on tariff ceilings, in its case of up to 12.5%.

Britain said the move would have no negative effects.

“There is no negative change to the tariff rate facing UK businesses as a result of this announcement. Our agreement with the US remains in place, and today we see an improvement to our trading terms with zero tariffs on whisky and medical technology,” a government spokesperson said.

Trump administration officials have told Chinese counterparts they intend to rebuild Trump’s second-term tariffs on Chinese goods back up to the 20% that was agreed upon in a trade truce with Chinese President Xi Jinping in November 2025 – but not exceed that level. Prior to Friday’s action, China’s tariff rate had fallen to 10%, excluding the 25% imposed during Trump’s first term on industrial goods.

Widely telegraphed move with exemptions

The action drew stronger protests from some trade partners.

Australia and Brazil described the new tariffs as unjustified and said they would seek to have them removed, while Norway said there was “no basis” for them.

Canada — hit on Monday with new Trump tariffs on $20 billion worth of goods — issued a muted response.

“We will continue engaging constructively with the United States on this matter, as well as other outstanding issues, over the coming weeks to the mutual benefit of our citizens,” said Dominic LeBlanc, Canada’s minister in charge of US trade.

Kelly Ann Shaw, a former White House trade adviser in Trump’s first term and a partner with the Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld law firm, said the new tariffs tracked what had been telegraphed, although some changes had been made, including the addition of some 471 products to an exclusion list.

“I think this is more status quo in terms of the economic impact,” she said.

Many goods will be exempted from the duties, including oil and gas, fertilizer, certain foodstuffs and goods already subject to Section 232 national security tariffs, such as autos, steel, aluminum and copper, the official said. Aircraft and parts will also be exempted, along with critical minerals.

There were some winners.

The Antwerp World Diamond Centre said the restored exemption was significant news for the local diamond sector. Belgium exported $2.1 billion of polished diamonds to the United States in 2024. The exemption had lapsed after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February. – with reports from Bea Cupin/Rappler.com

World.title: ICC members to vote on dismissing prosecutor Khan
World.content:
Prosecutor Karim Khan denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers call the decision by the court's governing body procedurally unfair and unsupported by evidence

THE HAGUE, Netherlands – International Criminal Court member states are set to vote on Friday, July 24, on whether to dismiss the court’s chief prosecutor Karim Khan for alleged sexual misconduct.

Khan, 56, denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers have called the decision by the court’s governing body that led to Friday’s vote unlawful, procedurally unfair and unsupported by evidence.

The vote comes amid renewed US criticism of the war crimes court which Washington sees as a threat to its sovereignty.

If ICC member states dismiss Khan, it will be seen by his supporters as the result of political pressure after the prosecutor sought arrest warrants for senior Israeli officials for alleged war crimes committed in Gaza. Israel denies war crimes, is not a member of the court and has dismissed the warrants as bogus.

Even if Khan survives the vote, his position would be weakened and it would give critics of the court — established in 2002 by the international community to prosecute war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity — another stick to beat it with.

Rubio decries ‘lunatics’ at the court

During a visit to the Philippines on Thursday, July 23, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there were “lunatics and crazies involved in the ICC” and there was no way any US political or military officials would ever go on trial at the court, reiterating previous criticism.

The US, which is also not a member, has already imposed sanctions on 11 ICC judges and prosecutors, including Khan, citing the ICC’s arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, and a past probe into US troops in Afghanistan.

Officials from the court’s governing body have said Khan should be dismissed because he committed serious misconduct by having an inappropriate sexual relationship with a junior staff member, according to documents seen by Reuters.

For Khan to be fired, an absolute majority of at least 63 of the court’s 125 member states will have to agree in the secret ballot to be held at a meeting at the UN headquarters in New York. The vote is due around 3 pm (1900 GMT) and the result is expected to be announced at 5:30 pm (2130 GMT).

France said on Thursday it would vote in favor of the removal of Khan, who has been suspended since June, after being on voluntary leave since May 2025 while awaiting the outcome of the internal investigation.

The Netherlands, which hosts the court in The Hague, has also said it would support his dismissal.

Election process begins if Khan removed

Khan’s accuser, a junior ICC staffer, spoke publicly for the first time last week in an interview with CNN in which she repeated her allegations that the prosecutor had a nonconsensual sexual relationship with her.

Lawyers for Khan told Reuters he denied “any sexual relationship of any kind” with the staff member.

If Khan is fired, that would immediately trigger the election process for a new ICC prosecutor who is not expected to be voted in before next year.

Any active ICC warrants will remain in place even if Khan is dismissed because only ICC judges have the authority to withdraw warrants. – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: NBI agent Calilung not arrested after VP Sara trial testimony
World.content:
There is no warrant or report of an arrest made after NBI agent John Mark Calilung testified as the first witness in the Vice President's impeachment trial

Claim: Senior National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agent John Mark Calilung, the first witness in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, has been arrested.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube channel named “PHILIPPINES TRENDING NEWS” uploaded a video containing the claim on July 12.

The video is titled “Kinarma na! Kakapasok lang, matinding utos, Senado, pirmado na? Wala [nang] takas; huli, NBI witness kulong?”

(Karma has struck! Just in: Major Senate order signed? No escape, NBI witness caught, jailed?)

Its thumbnail, which shows images of Calilung and Duterte, also bears the text, “Kulong na ngayon lang, NBI witness, arestado na?” (Jailed just now? NBI witness already arrested?)

As of writing, the video has garnered over 28,000 views and 1,100 likes.

The facts: Calilung was never arrested or jailed following his testimony before the Senate impeachment court on July 7 and the cross-examination by one of Duterte’s defense counsel, Carlo Narvasa, on July 8. The NBI agent was not detained by authorities nor was an arrest warrant issued for him right after his appearance at the trial.

The video’s central claim is also unsupported by its own content. Rather than presenting evidence that Calilung was arrested, the video recycles political commentary from Duterte-aligned political vlogger Banat By, largely talking about Calilung’s testimony and questioning his credibility.

At no point does the narration claim or discuss that Calilung had been arrested or detained.

The first witness: Calilung served as the prosecution’s primary witness to authenticate a November 2024 video from a press conference held by the Duterte, in which she allegedly made grave threats against the President. These form the basis of Article IV of the impeachment complaint against her.

As an officer of the NBI’s Cybercrime Division, Calilung explained how investigators preserved and authenticated footage in which Duterte allegedly said that, should anything happen to her, an assassin was prepared to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then-House speaker Martin Romualdez. (READ: Sara Duterte: If I get killed, so will Marcos, Liza Araneta, Romualdez)

During cross-examination, Duterte’s defense questioned Calilung’s qualifications as a digital forensic examiner, prompting Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to direct Calilung to submit his certifications.

The grave threats charge is one of four articles of impeachment against Duterte. The others allege the misuse of confidential and intelligence funds, culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust — including allegations of unexplained wealth — and bribery and corruption. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: China uses water cannons on Philippine ships 2 days in a row
World.content:
WATER CANNONS AGAIN. A China Coast Guard ships uses water cannons against a PCG vessel in Bajo de Masinloc on Friday, July 24.

Another Philippine mission to Bajo de Masinloc in the West Philippine Sea is met with the China Coast Guard’s water cannons just as high-level ASEAN events in Manila wrap up

MANILA, Philippines — At least three Philippine vessels were hit by water cannons from their Chinese counterparts during a mission to Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) on Friday morning, July 24. It was the second straight day that the China Coast Guard used water cannons against Philippine vessels near the feature, which Beijing has controlled access to since 2012.

In a release, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said two CCG ships hit the PCG’s BRP Cape San Agustin and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) vessel BRP Datu Paduhinog within an hour and a half of each other Friday, between 6:26 am and 7:53 am.

The Philippine ships were sailing as close as 10 to 15 nautical miles away from Bajo de Masinloc, a high-tide elevation just over 100 nautical miles from the Philippine mainland.

Before 9 am on Friday, a CCG ship trained its water cannon on another BFAR vessel, BRP Datu Cabaylo.

The CCG ships also used dangerous manuevers on — or sailed dangerously and aggressively close to — the Philippine vessels.

The PCG said a Chinese Maritime Militia ship was monitored “pulling a rope” some 100 meters ahead of the BFAR’s BRP Datu Sumakwel, “[posing] a hazard to the vessel’s safe navigation.”

The PCG said personnel were safe and the vessels went ahead with their mission to bring fuel subsidies and provisions to Filipino fisherfolk in the area.

As of 9:30 am, there were at least 12 CCG vessels and 3 Chinese Maritime Militia ships. The Philippines, meanwhile, deployed 3 PCG ships and 7 BFAR vessels.

“The PCG strongly condemns the dangerous and unprofessional actions of the China Coast Guard. Bajo de Masinloc is an integral part of the Philippine territory, and its surrounding waters form part of the country’s territorial sea and exclusive economic zone. The 2016 Arbitral Award has affirmed that Bajo de Masinloc is a traditional fishing ground of Filipino fisherfolk, whose rights cannot be lawfully impeded by any foreign power,” said the PCG.

Just a day prior, on July 23, the CCG also used water cannons on PCG and BFAR ships.

It’s been a week of tense confrontations between the Philippines and China in the West Philippine Sea, a part of the South China Sea that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

On July 20, CCG personnel entered Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, where the rusting BRP Sierra Madre has been aground since 1999. A tense confrontation between the CCG and Philippine soldiers led to the injuries, including a head wound on one Filipino.

The Philippines and China have traded protests over the Ayungin incident, including during a bilateral meeting between their foreign ministers on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meetings in Manila. – Rappler.com

World.title: PH to keep engaging US after new tariff on exports – Palace
World.content:
Palace press officer Claire Castro File photo

MANILA, Philippines — The Marcos administration will continue engaging with the United States after Washington imposed an additional 12.5 percent tariff on Philippine exports, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said Friday.

Article continues after this 

In a Viber message, Castro said the government respects the US decision and will continue discussions while assessing the impact of the new tariff on Philippine exports.

READ: US slaps Philippine exports with new 12.5% tariff

“We take note of the US decision and respect its processes. During the review, however, we emphasized that the Philippines has a strong policy against forced labor,” Castro said.

She added that the government had been informed of a Joint Administrative Order signed on Thursday establishing a mechanism to prevent the importation of products made through forced labor.

“We will continue engaging with the US while reviewing the coverage of the exemptions and their impact on Philippine exports,” she said.

Article continues after this 

The additional tariff came after the Office of the United States Trade found that the Philippines “has failed to impose and effectively enforce a forced-labor import prohibition” after several months of investigating 60 economies to determine whether they effectively prohibit the importation of goods produced through forced labor.

“The United States has had a forced labor import ban for nearly a century, and rigorously enforces it; it’s well past time for our trading partners to do the same,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement.

Article continues after this 

Philippine exports to the US reached $13.44 billion in 2025, down from $14.5 billion in 2024, but still accounted for 15.9 percent of the country’s total exports./dp

World.title: PCG rescues 20 flood-stranded residents in Guimaras, Antique
World.content:
ILOILO CITY – Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel rescued 20 residents, including children, who were trapped by floodwaters during separate rescue operations in Guimaras and Antique just before dawn on Friday, July 24, as relentless rains triggered by the southwest monsoon and Tropical Storm Kiyapo inundated several communities in Western Visayas.

The Coast Guard said three families composed of 20 individuals were safely evacuated from flooded areas in Jordan, Guimaras, and Hamtic, Antique.

Article continues after this 

In Sitio Nabagatan, Barangay Poblacion, Jordan, Guimaras, rescuers brought to safety a family of 10 after rising floodwaters surrounded their home at around 2:40 a.m.

Another rescue operation was carried out at 4 a.m. along the boundary of Barangays Guintas and Funda in Hamtic, Antique, where two families composed of 10 individuals became stranded after rapidly rising floodwaters cut off their evacuation routes.

Photos released by the Coast Guard showed rescue personnel carrying children on their shoulders, escorting residents through waist-deep floodwaters, and using flotation devices and lifebuoys to safely move evacuees to higher ground despite heavy rain and darkness.

The operations came as heavy monsoon rains continued to batter Western Visayas, prompting widespread flooding, rescue missions, sea travel suspensions, and class cancellations in several provinces./dp

World.title: Angara fast-tracks hiring of 10,000 school counselor associates
World.content:
Education Secretary Sonny Angara

MANILA, Philippines — Moving to address a long-standing shortage in learner mental health services, Education Secretary Sonny Angara has spearheaded the official rollout of the nationwide recruitment of 10,000 School Counselor Associate I (SCA I) positions, marking a major milestone in the implementation of Republic Act (RA) No. 12080, or the Basic Education Mental Health and Well-being Promotion Act.

The nationwide hiring follows the issuance of DepEd Order No. 019, s. 2026, which formally adopted the Civil Service Commission’s (CSC) approved Qualification Standards (QS) under CSC Resolution No. 2600920.

READ: DepEd earns clean audit opinion under Angara reform initiative

Article continues after this 

Schools Division Offices (SDOs) that have received their Notice of Organization, Staffing, and Classification Action (NOSCA) were directed to immediately begin filling the entry-level positions.

To streamline operations and accelerate recruitment nationwide, DepEd mandated that all SDOs conduct the entire recruitment process through the Agile Gateway for Appointments and Placements (AGAP) System, the Department’s digital recruitment platform. The system enables online publication of vacancies, electronic submission of applications, automated processing of documentary requirements, and appointment generation, significantly reducing processing time and administrative burden.

Recognizing that not all applicants have immediate access to digital facilities, SDOs were also instructed to establish physical assistance kiosks and help desks in their respective offices to assist walk-in applicants with account creation, requirement registration, and document uploading.

“Hindi lang ito tungkol sa pagpuno ng mga plantilla positions. Napakahalaga ng pag-hire natin ng mga School Counselor Associates dahil sila ang magiging kaagapay ng ating mga mag-aaral sa pang-araw-araw nilang mental health at psychosocial needs,” Angara said.

“Tugon din ito sa utos ni Pangulong Bongbong Marcos na gawing tunay na sentro ng kalinga at proteksyon ang ating mga paaralan. Sa tulong ng ating bagong digital system, ginawa nating mas mabilis at accessible ang recruitment para agad silang makapagsimula nang walang bureaucratic delays,” Angara added.

Article continues after this 

The initiative expands the school-based mental health workforce through the creation and deployment of School Counselor Associate positions. School Counselor Associates will provide basic mental health services, learner support, documentation, referral, and other related functions, thereby helping address persistent staffing gaps in public schools. Their deployment complements the specialized guidance and counseling services provided by Registered Guidance Counselors.

Beyond expanding the workforce, RA 12080 institutionalizes a career progression pathway from School Counselor Associate I to V, with opportunities to advance to School Counselor I to IV and eventually Schools Division Counselor, subject to meeting the prescribed qualifications, including professional licensure.

Article continues after this 

Under DepEd’s compressed timeline, the end-to-end recruitment process will move on an accelerated schedule upon an SDO’s receipt of its NOSCA.

For the School Counselor Associate I position, applicants must hold a Bachelor’s Degree in Guidance and Counseling or Psychology; or any Bachelor’s Degree with at least 18 units in Guidance and Counseling or Psychology; or any related Bachelor’s Degree with at least 18 units in Behavioral Science courses, inclusive of 200 hours of supervised practicum or internship experience on guidance and counseling, preferably in a school or community setting. No prior experience or additional training is required. Applicants must possess Career Service Professional (Second Level) Eligibility.

With the deployment of the initial 10,000 School Counselor Associates, DepEd moves closer to fully operationalizing RA 12080 and strengthening a comprehensive school-based mental health system that ensures learners receive timely, accessible, and professional psychosocial support for public basic education.

World.title: DepEd earns clean audit opinion under Angara reform initiative
World.content:
PHOTO FROM Agence France-Presse/INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) has significantly improved its compliance with Commission on Audit (COA) recommendations, resolving 83% of its outstanding audit findings in 2025, up from 52% the previous year, as governance reforms under Education Secretary Sonny Angara continue to take effect.

According to COA’s consolidated annual audit report for the year ended December 31, 2025, the Department fully addressed 307 of 368 valid prior-year audit recommendations, marking substantial progress in strengthening institutional accountability, internal controls, and financial stewardship.

The dramatic jump to an 83% implementation rate marks a key structural improvement over previous audit periods, where DepEd recorded 56% in 2022, 54% in 2023, and 52% in 2024.

Article continues after this 

Marking his second year leading the department, Secretary Angara credited DepEd personnel for prioritizing fiscal discipline and system-wide cleanup.

READ: DepEd completes partnerships with provinces to ease classroom shortage

“Fixing long-standing audit issues isn’t just an accounting exercise—it’s about operational integrity and fulfilling President Bongbong Marcos’s mandate for transparent, accountable governance,” Angara said.

“Moving our action rate from 52% to 83% shows that we are serious about safeguarding public funds. Under the Marcos administration, responsible budget management directly affects the speed and efficiency with which resources reach our classrooms, teachers, and learners,” Angara added.

The milestone comes alongside DepEd securing an Unmodified Audit Opinion from COA for the third consecutive year—the highest rating issued by state auditors, indicating that the agency’s financial statements were fairly presented, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

Article continues after this 

Out of a total pool of 882 prior-year audit observations tracked by COA, state auditors formally closed 345 items and updated or revised another 169 for ongoing compliance actions.

DepEd’s 83% success rate reflects the 307 fully implemented recommendations out of the 368 actionable recommendations, with only 61 remaining for full implementation.

Article continues after this 

DepEd reiterated its commitment to collaborate closely with COA to resolve all remaining audit findings, reinforcing institutional transparency across all regional offices and school divisions nationwide.

World.title: Manila Water’s three major water systems keep East Zone supply reliable
World.content:
The 100MLD Cardona Treatment Plant, part of Manila Water’s Laguna Lake Water System

MANILA, Philippines – Manila Water continues to provide reliable 24/7 water service to customers through a diversified supply portfolio anchored on three major water systems: the Angat-La Mesa Water System, the Laguna Lake Water System, and the Antipolo Water System.

The company’s long-term investments in these water sources have strengthened supply reliability despite challenges brought by El Niño, declining water levels in Angat Dam, and increasing demand across its service area.

The 80MLD Calawis Water Treatment Plant, a key component of Manila Water’s Antipolo Water System

“As we experience the full effects of a strong El Niño and the pressures it places on traditional water sources, our diversified supply systems provide greater resilience and flexibility in meeting the needs of our customers. These strategic investments help ensure that communities across the East Zone continue to have access to safe and dependable water services today and in the years ahead,” said Dittie Galang, Manila Water Corporate Communications Group Head.

Article continues after this 

READ: Manila Water facilities among first under 100-kW RAP threshold

The Angat-La Mesa Water System remains a critical source of water for Metro Manila. To improve supply reliability, Manila Water, in partnership with the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System, invested in projects that help ensure sufficient inflows to Angat Reservoir, including the Sumag River Diversion Project and the rehabilitation of the Umiray-Angat Transbasin Project.

Complementing Angat is the Laguna Lake Water System, which taps Laguna de Bay as an additional water source. The system includes the 100-million-liter-per-day (MLD) Cardona Water Treatment Plant, which draws water from the central portion of the lake and serves around 800,000 customers in Rizal and nearby areas. On the eastern side of the lake, the P16.5-billion East Bay Water Supply Project is being developed. Its first phase, the 50-MLD East Bay Water Treatment Plant, is designed to serve up to 390,000 customers and currently supplies communities in eastern Rizal. The 200-MLD East Bay Phase 2 Water Treatment Plant, which is set for completion this year, will serve approximately two million customers in Pasig, Pateros, Taguig, and portions of Rizal province.

Meanwhile, the Antipolo Water System supports the growing water requirements of Rizal through the Wawa-Calawis System, which is anchored on the recently acquired 710-MLD Upper Wawa Dam. Its 80-MLD Calawis Water Treatment Plant, designed to serve about 900,000 customers, already provides water service to communities in Antipolo City and nearby areas. The 220-MLD Kaysakat Water Treatment Plant is expected to be completed later this year and will source water from Upper Wawa Dam. It will further boost water supply for approximately one million customers in Antipolo and neighboring Rizal municipalities.

Together, these three major water systems form a resilient and diversified supply network that enables Manila Water to continuously deliver safe, reliable, and sustainable water services to its more than 7.9 million customers in the East Zone.

World.title: Romualdez camp says ex-speaker always ready to face complaints
World.content:
Former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez. FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — The lawyer of Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has maintained that the former speaker of the House of Representatives has been always ready to face the possible cases against him, as they are confident that they will be able to defend their innocence.

In a statement on Friday, lawyer Elaine Atienza said that if there will be a fair judgement of evidence presented against Romualdez, the lawmaker will be able to prove his claim that he is not involved in any wrongdoing.

“Like what we have said even before, Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez is prepared to face any complaint against him,” Atienza said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Ombudsman: Bonoan’s state witness bid made to pin down Romualdez

“We believe that if there will be a fair fight and a fair judgment based on evidence, Rep. Romualdez will prove his claims. We just ask the public to let the process prevail and let evidence decide the case,” he added.

Atienza’s claims came after the Office of the Ombudsman’s special panel of prosecturos released copies of a 104-page supplemental complaint-affidavit against Romualdez, which accuses the former Speaker of allegedly funneling billions of pesos in kickbacks from infrastructure projects through a network of beneficially-owned shell companies.

READ: Romualdez’s lawyer insists: No probe showed his links to infra mess

According to the special panel, they are recommending the filing of plunder, direct and indirect bribery, money laundering and graft against Romualdez and his co-respondents before the Sandiganbayan.

Article continues after this 

Prosecutors accused Romualdez and former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co of “concerted and coordinated acts” in “unlawfully amassing, accumulating, and acquiring ill-gotten wealth” amounting to approximately P56 billion from 2022 to 2025.

These amounts were mostly delivered for Romualdez by Co’s bodyguards, through usage of suitcases, according to prosecutors.

Article continues after this 

According to the special panel, additional evidence revealed that “several corporate entities appear to have been utilized as conduits for the diversion and disposition of substantial amounts of funds through the abuse of public office and the use of dummies, nominees and closely-held corporations.”

Among the companies mentioned were Golden Pheasant Holdings Corporation, Clearspring Holdings Corporation, Brightnews Corporation, Braavos Holdings OPC, and Valiant Consolidated Resources Inc.

Prosecutors said these companies are either linked to or had a lawyer and fraternity brother of Romualdez.

“The records point to no conclusion other than that Romualdez, through [his fraternity brother], transacted the proceeds of the aforementioned unlawful activities through Golden Pheasant, Clearspring, Brightnews, Braavos and Valiant,” the prosecutors said.

Romualdez has been accused of involvement in the budget mess and the alleged manipulation of funds for infrastructure corruption. However, this is not the first time that the former Speaker’s camp reiterated their willingness to face the cases, or claimed that no investigation was able to show his links to the two issues.

Last July 2, Atienza herself maintained that attempts to link the Leyte-based solon to the said budgeting issues “are not supported by evidence” as the former Speaker cannot have total control of the entire budget process.

Atienza said this after Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano admitted that the decision to tap former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan as state witness was made in order to strengthen their case against Romualdez.

Atienza also said that not even Bonoan has implicated Romualdez in past investigations and congressional hearings, simply because the lawmaker was not involved in the anomalous insertions.

Then last July 9, Romualdez’s spokesperson Ade Fajardo said that Bonoan might have been pressured to testify regarding the infrastructure corruption scandal as he may be transferred to an ordinary jail facility.

According to Fajardo, the possibility of being moved away from hospital arrest once he is medically-cleared may have been weighing on Bonoan’s mind, especially with his advanced age — hence the pressure to testify against Romualdez.

World.title: Kazakh FM Urges More Practical SCO as Global Turbulence Reshapes Regional Priorities
World.content:
27739

ALMATY – The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is increasingly shifting from a platform centered on political dialogue and regional security toward one that places greater emphasis on economic resilience, trade connectivity and practical cooperation, as member states respond to growing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions.

That transformation was at the center of discussions during the July 24 meeting of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers in Cholpon-Ata, the Kyrgyz Republic, where Kazakhstan called for stronger coordination on trade security, transport connectivity, climate resilience and water management ahead of the organization’s summit in Bishkek on Sept. 1.

Speaking at the meeting, Kazakh Foreign Minister Yermek Kosherbayev said that the rapidly changing geopolitical environment is making economic resilience an urgent priority for the region.

“Geopolitical turbulence, increasingly spilling over into the military sphere, is seriously affecting the stability of international trade relations. Today, the security of supply chains is becoming an ever more pressing issue, including for Kazakhstan,” he said.

Kosherbayev cited attacks by unidentified unmanned systems on energy infrastructure and tankers chartered by Kazakhstan to transport oil as an illustration of growing vulnerabilities affecting international logistics. He said that these risks underscore the need for the SCO to make the protection of regional trade routes one of its strategic priorities.

The emphasis on supply-chain security reflects a broader shift in Kazakhstan’s regional diplomacy. As global trade routes face growing disruption from geopolitical tensions and attacks on critical infrastructure, Astana is increasingly framing transport connectivity not only as an economic objective but also as a strategic security issue.

Analysts say Kazakhstan’s priorities reflect broader changes taking place within the SCO itself. According to Manarbek Kabaziyev, deputy chairman of the board of the Foreign Policy Research Institute under Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry, the organization itself is undergoing a broader transformation.

“The SCO is indeed going through a stage of qualitative transformation. While its primary task in the early years was strengthening trust and ensuring regional security, today its agenda has become much broader. The focus now includes trade and economic cooperation, transport and logistics connectivity, digitalization, energy, food security and technological cooperation,” he said.

That assessment closely aligns with Kazakhstan’s own priorities within the organization. Alongside transport security, Kosherbayev called for deeper cooperation on climate adaptation and sustainable water management, reiterating Kazakhstan’s proposal to establish an International Water Organization under the auspices of the United Nations and an SCO Water Issues Analysis Center.

The minister also emphasized that the SCO should continue adapting its institutions to contemporary challenges, reflecting Kazakhstan’s broader push to make regional organizations more responsive to economic and technological change.

For Kazakhstan, Kabaziyev said, the shift toward project-oriented cooperation carries particular strategic significance.

“Kazakhstan’s geographic position and its role as one of Eurasia’s key transit hubs objectively make the country one of the main beneficiaries of projects aimed at developing transport connectivity, digital logistics and regional value chains,” he said.

According to him, whether the SCO succeeds in making that transition will likely become one of the defining questions for the organization over the coming years.

Attention will now shift to the Sept. 1 SCO summit in Bishkek, where the organization’s heads of state are expected to define the bloc’s strategic priorities. The extent to which leaders embrace Kazakhstan’s calls for stronger economic coordination and practical cooperation may offer an early test of whether the SCO is indeed evolving beyond its traditional security agenda.

World.title: Kazakhstan Rises to 53rd in Updated Global Investment Risk and Resilience Index
World.content:
32793

ASTANA – Kazakhstan ranked 53rd out of 150 countries in the May 2026 Special Edition of the Global Investment Risk and Resilience Index (GIRRI), improving from 70th place in the original 2025 ranking, as the updated index reflects the impact of recent geopolitical and economic developments on global investment risk.

The updated ranking was released by Henley & Partners in cooperation with AlphaGeo and incorporates Country Risk Premium (CRP) data as of April 1, allowing the index to combine long-term structural resilience with real-time market assessments of sovereign risk.

The Global Investment Risk and Resilience Index evaluates countries using two core dimensions: structural resilience, which measures long-term economic, institutional and environmental strengths, and sovereign risk, reflecting exposure to political, financial and external shocks, according to Henley & Partners.

The May 2026 Special Edition does not revise the original methodology or resilience scores. Instead, it serves as a stress test of the existing framework by keeping structural resilience unchanged while updating the risk component with current market data.

According to the report, the revised rankings provide a risk-adjusted view of the global investment environment, showing how geopolitical and economic developments have reshaped investor perceptions.

The report notes that changes in country rankings reflect relative shifts in position compared with other countries rather than absolute improvements or deterioration in risk or resilience. The update is intended to illustrate how the global investment landscape is evolving as markets respond to current geopolitical and economic conditions.
